Mālik did not raise his hands in the qunut. Ash-Shafi'i recommends it and says that it should take place after rukū', while Mālik says before.

f: What formulas are prescribed for glorification in rukūʿ and sujūd, what do the schools say about saying them once or three times, and what are their positions concerning the takbīrs and the order of placing the knees and hands?
b: Glorification in the prayer: They agree that the glorification in rukū' is, "Glory be to my Lord, the Immense" (subhāna rabbi'l-azīm), and in sujud it is, "Glory be to my Lord the Most High" (subhāna rabbi'l-a'lā). Saying, "Allah hears...", "Our Lord, praise is Yours", and asking for forgiveness between sajdas and the takbirs is also prescribed. Three say that they are sunna. Ahmad says that they are mandatory once. Repeating the formula three times is the best. They agree that the takbirs are part of the prayer, but it is reported that Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that the first takbir is not. The sunna with three is to put the knees down before the hands in sujūd. Mālik says that the hands should be put down before the knees.

f: What do the schools say about concealing the private parts, whether it is a condition for prayer, and which parts of the male and female body constitute the ʿawra?
b: Private parts: Concealing the private parts from others is mandatory by consensus. It is a precondition for the validity of the prayer, except with Malik who says it is mandatory for the prayer, but not a precondition for its validity. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and ash-Shafi'i say that the private parts of a man are everything between the navel and the knees. Two things are reported from Malik and Ahmad, one of which is the same as the others, and the other that it is only the genitals themselves. They agree that a man's navel is not one of the private parts. Mālik, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say that the knees do not constitute private parts. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and some Shafi'ītes say that they do. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that private parts of a free woman comprise her whole body apart from the face, palms and feet. He also says in one report that the feet are included as well. Malik and ash-Shafi'i say everything except for her face and palms. Two things are reported from Ahmad. One is everything except the face and palms, and the well-known one is everything except the face.

f: What are the positions of Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, ash-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and Mālik concerning exposing the private parts during prayer, including the amount of exposure that invalidates the prayer, covering the shoulders, and praying without clothes?
b: Exposing the private parts: Does exposing the private parts invalidate the prayer? Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that if an area of the genitals the size of a dirham is exposed, the prayer is not invalid, and if less than a quarter of the thigh is uncovered, the prayer is not invalid. Ash-Shafi'i says that the prayer is invalidated by the exposure of any of the private parts whatsoever. Ahmad says that if a little comes exposed, the prayer is not invalid, but if it is a lot it is. A little is what is normally considered to be a little. Mālik says that if someone is aware of being exposed and is able to cover his private parts and still prays with the private parts exposed, then his prayer is invalid. Ahmad made it obligatory to cover the shoulders in the prayer. If a person has no clothes, according to Malik and ash-Shafi'i, he can pray standing, bowing and prostrating and his prayer is valid. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that he may pray sitting or standing. Ahmad says he should pray sitting down and indicate the other positions with his head.

f: What are the positions of the four schools concerning purity of clothing, body, and place, ritual purity, praying behind an imam who is in janāba or has minor impurity, and knowledge of the prayer time?
b: Purity: They agree that purity of the clothing, body and place of the person praying is mandatory. It is a precondition for the validity of the prayer with Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, ash-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and there are three transmissions from Malik, the best known of which is that if someone prays knowing about the impurity, his prayer is not valid. If he is ignorant or forgets, it is valid. Purity from ritual impurity is a precondition for the validity of the prayer by consensus. If someone leads people in the prayer while in janāba, his prayer is invalid without dispute, whether he knows that he is in janāba at the moment he begins or forgets. If the one following knows his imam in janāba, his prayer is invalid. If he does not know, his prayer is valid according to ash-Shafi'i and Malik, while Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says it is invalid. If it is a question of minor impurity, then the prayer is invalid according to ash-Shafi'i, Malik and Ahmad. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that the prayer is not invalid and that the imam should do wudū' and continue the prayer. They agree that purity of the body is a precondition for the prayer when it is possible. Knowledge that the time has come or its probability is also a precondition of the prayer, except in the case of Malik who says that the precondition is knowledge not probability.

f: What are the positions of the four schools concerning facing the qibla, including valid excuses, voluntary prayer while travelling, determining the qibla while travelling, and repeating a prayer performed in a direction later discovered to be wrong?
b: Facing the qibla: They agree that facing the qibla is a precondition for the validity of the prayer, except if there is a valid excuse, such as intense fear in war, or in voluntary prayers for a traveller on a long journey on a mount, although he should face qibla to begin and for the takbīr al-ihrām. The person praying while resident must face qibla. If he is travelling, he should use his discretion, information and following the people where he is. If someone prays in a direction he thinks is right and then finds out that he is wrong, only ash-Shafi'i says he has to repeat it.

f: What are the positions of the four schools concerning speech in prayer, including speech from forgetfulness or ignorance, eating and drinking, correcting the imam, answering a greeting, and someone passing in front of the person praying?
b: Speaking in the prayer: If someone speaks or greets someone in his prayer out of forgetfulness or ignorance of the prohibition or his tongue runs ahead, but it is not a lot, the prayer is not invalidated according to all but Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ who says that the prayer is invalidated by any speech except for the salām. If he speaks a lot, then the sound position with ash-Shafi'i is that the prayer is invalid. Malik says that if the words are deliberate in order to put right the prayer such as informing the imam of forgetfulness if that is the only way to get his attention, it is not invalid. They agree that the prayer is invalidated by eating, as is the case with drinking, except for Ahmad in the voluntary prayer. If the imam does something wrong in the prayer, a man should say "Glory be to Allah" (subhānallāh) and a woman should clap. Mālik says that all should say "Glory be to Allah". If someone conveys permission or warning by saying that the prayer is not invalidated, although Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is unless he intends to alert the imam or to prevent someone from passing in front of him. If a person praying is greeted, he may answer by gesture, but it is agreed that it is not obligatory for him to do so. If someone passes in front of the person praying, it does not invalidate his prayer, even if it is a menstruating woman, a donkey or a black dog although Ahmad says that a black dog does invalidate the prayer.

f: What are the positions of Mālik, ash-Shafi'i, and Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ concerning a man praying beside a woman, and what is the ruling on killing snakes and scorpions during prayer?
b: Other matters: Malik and ash-Shafi'i permit a man to pray with a woman at his side. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it invalidates the man's prayer. It is not disliked to kill snakes and scorpions during the prayer.

f: What are the positions of Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Mālik, ash-Shafi'i, and Ahmad concerning praying in the seven forbidden places of prayer and whether the prayer is valid there?
b: Forbidden places of prayer: They disagree about the places in which it is forbidden to pray and whether or not the prayer is invalid in them. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says it is disliked but if someone does pray in such a place, his prayer is still valid. Mālik says that the prayer in such places is valid, even if it is clearly disliked because one can rarely be safe from impurity there. Ash-Shafi'i says that the prayer in them is valid but disliked, except for cemeteries when there are open graves, in which case the prayer is not valid. If there are no open graves, it is disliked but allowed. The well-known position of Ahmad is that the prayer in them is invalid. The places are seven: cemeteries, slaughterhouses, rubbish heaps, bathhouses, roadways, camel pens and on top of the Ka'ba.

f: What are the positions of Ahmad, the Hanafis, Mālik, and ash-Shafi'i concerning the obligation or sunnah status of the sajda of forgetfulness, and when is it performed?
b: The sajda of forgetfulness: They agree that the sajda of forgetfulness is prescribed in the prayer and puts it right after a mistake and then they disagree. Ahmad and some Hanafis say that it is mandatory. Mālik says that it is obligatory if something is missing from the prayer and sunna if something is added. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and ash-Shafi'i say that it is sunna absolutely. They agree that if someone omits it out of forgetfulness, his prayer is not invalid, except for one report from Ahmad. They disagree about when it should be done. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it should be done after the salām. Mālik says that if it is for missing something, it is done before the salām, and if it is for adding something, it is after it. If there is addition and omission, then it is done before the salām. Ash-Shafi'i says that it is always done before the salām. Ahmad says it is done before the salām, unless it is for accidental omission of something in the prayer or when there is uncertainty about the number of rak'ats prayed, in which case you should build on what is probable and prostrate after the salām.

f: What do Mālik, ash-Shafi'i, and Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ say about what to do when there is uncertainty about the number of rak'ats prayed?
b: Uncertainty about number of rak'ats: If the imam is unsure about the number of rak'ats prayed, he builds on what he is certain about in the view of Malik and ash-Shafi'i and that is also the position of Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ with someone praying alone. He has two positions about the imam, one is the same as that and the second is that he should build on what is probable.

f: What are the positions of ash-Shafi'i, Mālik, Ahmad, and Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ concerning forgetting the first tashahhud, standing for an extra rak'at, forgetting the tashahhud in the fourth rak'at, rising for a third rak'at in a nafl prayer, and accidentally praying Maghrib with four rak'ats?
b: General forgetfulness: If someone forgets the first tashahhud and remembers after standing up, he should not go back to it according to ash-Shafi'i. If he remembers before reaching the upright position, he should return and do the sajda of forgetfulness. Mālik says that if his buttocks have left the ground, he should not go back. Ahmad says that if he remembers after standing up, but before reciting, he can choose, but it is most likely that he does not go back. If he stands for a fifth rak'at and then remembers, ash-Shafi'i says that he should sit down again. If he forgets the tashahhud in the fourth rak'at, he should say it in the fifth and do the sajda of forgetfulness. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that if he remembers before he goes into sujud in fifth rak'at, he should return to sitting. If someone is praying nafila prayer and rises for a third rak'at, there is no disagreement among the scholars that he can make it four or can return to two and do the salam and the sajda for forgetfulness. If he prays Maghrib with four rak'ats out of forgetfulness, he should do the sajda for forgetfulness and his prayer is allowed.

f: What are the positions of ash-Shafi'i, Ahmad, Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, and Mālik when an imam is told by those praying behind him that he has omitted a rak'at?
b: The position of imam: When the imam is told by those behind him that he has omitted a rak'at, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say that he should not accept it if he is certain, but acts according to his own certainty. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that he should accept what they say and there are various reports from Mālik.

f: What are the positions of ash-Shafi'i, Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, and Mālik concerning sajda al-sahw for omitting sunnahs and for mistakes in audible and silent recitation?
b: Omission of sunan: According to ash-Shafi'i, the sajda of forgetfulness is not done on account of omitting a sunna, except in the case of the qunut, the first tashahhud and the prayer on the Prophet ﷺ. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that if the imam omits the takbirs of the 'id, he should do the sajda for forgetfulness. The imam should also do the sajda for forgetfulness for reciting outloud in a silent prayer and the reverse. Mālik says that if the imam recites outloud in a silent prayer, he should prostate after the salām and if he remains silent in a prayer which should be outloud, he should do the sajda for forgetfulness before the salām.

f: What are the rulings when forgetfulness occurs repeatedly, when a person forgets while praying behind an imam, and when the imam forgets or fails to perform sajda al-sahw?
b: Additional matters: If someone repeats the forgetfulness, the two sajdas are enough for all by consensus. If someone forgets behind an imam, he does not prostrate. If the Imam forgets, the follower is subject to his forgetfulness. If the Imam does not prostrate, Malil says that the follower should prostrate and that is the predominant view in the school of ash-Shafi'i and is one transmission from Ahmad.

f: What are the positions of the four schools concerning the number and status of the sajdas of recitation, the two sajdas in Sūrat al-Hajj, and the sajda in Sūrat Ṣād?
b: The sajdas of recitation The sajdas of recitation. They are sunna for both the reciter and the listener with three but Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that they are mandatory. The sajdas of recitation according to the predominant view of ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad are fourteen in number. There are two in Surat al-Hajj but Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik say that there is only one. There is a question about whether the sajda in Sūrat Ṣad is for thankfulness or recitation. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Malik and Ahmad, in one report, say that it is for recitation. Ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad in the well-known position say that it is a prostration of thankfulness recommended outside of the prayer. They agree that the Mufassal (the last part of the Qur'an) has three prostrations: in an-Najm, al-Inshiqaq and al-'Alaq except for Mālik who says that there is no prostration in the Mufassal. They agree about the rest of the ten prostrations in al-A'raf, ar-Ra'd, an-Nahl, al-Isra', Maryam, the first of al-Hajj, al-Furqan, an-Naml, as-Sajda and Fussilat.

f: What are the rulings concerning a non-praying reciter and listener, the preconditions of sajdat al-tilāwah, rukūʿ instead of prostration, reciting an āyat of sajda in prayer, following the imam in sajdat al-tilāwah, and the takbir and salām associated with it?
b: Various factors: If the reciter is not praying but the one who hears it, the listener does not prostrate then or afterwards, except in the view of Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ who says he should prostrate when he finishes the prayer. The preconditions of the prayer apply to it. Rukū' is not done according to three, while Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is recommended. It is not disliked for the imam to recite an āyat of sajda, according to ash-Shafi'i and Mālik. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is disliked when silent but not when aloud. Ahmad says that if he says it silently he does not prostrate. Ash-Shafi'i says that when the imam prostrates for recitation and the follower does not follow him, his prayer is invalid in the same way as it is when the follower omits the qunut with the imam. Ash-Shafi'ī says that in the sajda of recitation there is a takbir and salām without a tashahhud, which is the position of Ahmad. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Mālik say there is no salām.

f: What are the positions of ash-Shafi'i, Ahmad, Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, and Mālik concerning the sajda of thankfulness, and what should be said when reciting verses of mercy or punishment?
b: Sajda of thankfulness: Ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad recommend that someone who receives a blessing or wants to avert an affliction from himself should prostrate out of thankfulness to Allah Almighty. At-Tahāwī said that Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ did not believe that there was a sajda of thankfulness and ash-Shaybānī reported that it is disliked. Mālik says that it is disliked separate from the prayer. It is recommended that when a reciter recites an āyat of mercy, he should ask for it, and when he recites an āyat of punishment, he should seek refuge from it. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that doing so is disliked in the fard prayer.

f: What are the strongest regular sunnah prayers associated with the obligatory prayers, and what are the regular voluntary prayers and their rakʿat according to the four schools?
b: Voluntary Prayers The firmest of the sunna prayers performed with the fard prayer are the witr and the two rak'ats of Fajr. Malik and ash-Shafi'i think that the firmest of those is the witr, while Ahmad thinks it is the two rak'ats of Fajr. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that the witr is mandatory but not obligatory. They agree that the regular voluntary prayers are the two rak'ats of Fajr, two before and two after Zuhr, two after Maghrib and two after 'Ishā'. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and ash-Shafi'i say four before 'Aṣr while Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says two or four before Zuhr. Ash-Shafi'i says four after it. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says four or two after it. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says four before and four after 'Ishā' and that the sunna of the Jumu'a is four before and four after.

f: What is the sunnah method for performing supererogatory prayers during the day and night, and how many rakʿats may be joined with one salām according to Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ?
b: Form of prayer: The sunna in supererogatory prayers, both day and night, is to say the salām after every two rak'ats. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says you can pray two, four, six or eight rak'ats with one salām during the night, and four rak'ats during the day.

f: What are the minimum and maximum rakʿats of witr, how do the schools perform it, and what should a person do if he prays witr before tahajjud and then performs tahajjud later?
b: The witr: The minimum for the witr is one rak'at and the maximum is eleven rak'ats. The least for correctness is three with ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad. Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that the witr is three rak'ats with one taslīm, no more and no less. Mālik says that the witr is one rak'at with the shafa before it and separate from it. There is no maximum for the number of rak'ats before it but the minimum is two. If someone does the witr early and then tahajjud later, he does not have to repeat the witr in the soundest position of ash-Shafi'i, Malik and Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ. Ahmad says that he should make it even by doing one rak'at on its own and then repeat the witr later.

f: When is qunut performed in witr according to the four schools?
b: Qunut in the witr: The sunna is to do the qunut at the end of the witr in the second half of Ramadan with ash-Shafi'i and doing this is well-known with Malik. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad say that qunut done in the witr throughout the year. A group of Shafi'ites also say that.

f: What are the positions of Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, ash-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and Mālik concerning the status, number of rakʿats, salāms, and congregation of Tarāwīḥ in Ramadan?
b: Tarawih: Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say that doing the tarāwīh prayer in Ramadan is sunna. They say it should be twenty rak'ats with ten salāms and is best done in a group. There are reports from Malik of tarāwīh being eight, twenty and thirty-six rak'ats.

f: What are the positions of the four schools concerning making up missed fard prayers, making them up at disliked times, and a prayer whose time ends during its performance?
b: Making up missed fard prayers: They agree that it is obligatory to make up missed fard prayers, but they disagree about making them up at disliked times. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is not permitted. Mālik, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say that it is permitted. If the sun rises while someone is doing the Subh prayer, all except Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ say that the prayer is not invalid. They all agree that if the sun sets while someone is praying 'Aṣr, his prayer is valid.

f: What are the positions of ash-Shafi'i, Ahmad, Mālik, and Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ concerning making up missed regular sunna prayers?
b: Missing sunna prayers: If someone misses some of the regular sunnas, it is sunna, according to ash-Shafi'i, to make them up, even at disliked times, in the same way as fard prayers and this is one of two positions from Ahmad. Mālik says that they should not be made up. Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that they should be made up with the fard prayer if someone misses it.

f: What should a person do if he enters the mosque after the iqāma has been called, according to ash-Shafi'i, Ahmad, Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, and Mālik?
b: Arriving after the iqama: If someone enters the mosque after the iqāma, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say that he should not pray the greeting of the mosque or any other sunnas. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik say that if someone is certain not to miss the second rak'at of Subh, he should do the two rak'ats of Fajr before he enters the mosque.

f: What are the forbidden times for prayer according to Mālik, Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, ash-Shafi'i, and Ahmad, and what exceptions do the schools recognize for making up fard and reason-based voluntary prayers?
b: Forbidden times for prayer: The times at which Malik says the prayer is forbidden are after 'Aṣr until the sun sets and after Subh until sunrise. There is no prayer until after the sun has set or risen. Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and ash-Shafi'i add when the sun is at its zenith until it declines. Mālik and Ahmad say that you can make up the fard prayers in what is an otherwise prohibited time. Ash-Shafi'ī says that fard prayers can be made up at all times as well as voluntary prayers which have a reason, such as greeting the mosque, the two rak'ats of tawaf, the prostration of recitation, the vowed prayer, and the prayer for renewal of purity. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that during forbidden times it is not permitted to pray a fard, even if it is 'Aṣr for that day, when the sun is yellow. If someone misses Subh, he should not pray it at sunrise. If he does pray and the sun rises while he is doing it, it is invalid. If someone has prayed two rak'ats of Fajr, it is disliked for him to do nāfila prayers after that according to Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad. Malik says that it is not disliked. This is outside Makka. In Makka, Mālik and ash-Shafi'i say that nāfila is not disliked at those times while Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad say that it is.

f: What do the four schools say about the status of congregational prayer, the minimum number for congregation, the obligation of congregational prayer, praying alone when congregation is available, and congregational prayer for women?
b: Group prayer: They agree that the group prayer is prescribed and that it is obligatory to make it public. If everyone in a locality refuses to establish the group prayer, they should be fought until they do so. They agree that the minimum group for all obligatory prayers except Jumu'a is two: an imam and a follower standing at his right. Ahmad says that if the follower is one and stands on the imam's left, his prayer is invalid. They disagree about whether the group is obligatory in the fard prayers outside of Jumu'a. Ash-Shafi'i says that it is a general obligation. It is said that it is sunna and that is the best-known position. It is said that it is an individual obligation. The school of Malik is that it is sunna. Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is a fard kifaya. Some Hanbalīs say it is sunna. Ahmad says that it is mandatory for individuals but not a precondition for the validity of the prayer. If someone prays alone when he can join a group, the prayer is still valid. It is better for women to pray in their houses, but it is not disliked for them to pray in a group according to ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Mālik say that it is disliked to have a group prayer for women.

f: What are the positions of Mālik, ash-Shafi'i, Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, and Ahmad concerning the follower's intention to join the congregation, the imam's intention to lead, and changing from an individual prayer to a congregational prayer?
b: Intention: Followers must intend to be in a group, but the intention to act as imam is not obligatory. It is recommended by Malik and ash-Shafi'i, except for Jumu'a when it is obligatory. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that if there are women behind an imam, he must make an intention, but not if there are only men. Jumu'a, 'Arafa and the 'id are an exception. He says there must be an intention to be imam in these three cases. Ahmad says that the intention of the imam is a necessary precondition. If someone starts to pray a fard prayer alone and the iqama for the group prayer is given, it is agreed that he cannot stop and join the group. If he intends to join them without stopping his prayer, ash-Shafi'i has two views, the sounder of which is that it is sound to do so, and that is the best-known position from Malik and Ahmad. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is not sound.

f: How do the four schools classify the portion of the prayer caught by a latecomer with the imam, particularly regarding whether it is considered the beginning or end of the latecomer's prayer?
b: Catching the prayer: When someone catches a prayer, ash-Shafi'i says that he is at the beginning of his prayer in respect of action and judgement and so he should repeat the qunut. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that what the follower catches of the imam's prayer is the beginning of his prayer in respect of the tashahhuds but the end of it in respect of recitation. Malik says in the well-known position from him that it is the end of it and there are two positions from Ahmad.

f: What are the positions of Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Mālik, ash-Shafi'i, and Ahmad concerning establishing another congregation after the imam has finished, repeating a prayer after praying alone, and repeating a prayer after already praying in congregation?
b: Arriving after the group prayer: If someone enters the mosque and finds that the imam has finished the prayer, it is disliked for him to begin a new group there according to Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Mālik and ash-Shafi'i. Ahmad says that it is not disliked to hold a group prayer after a group in any case. If someone prays alone and then finds a group praying, ash-Shafi'i recommends that he should pray with them. Mālik says the same, except in respect of Maghrib. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that he should not repeat it, except in the case of Zuhr and 'Ishā'. Ash-Shafi'i says the first prayer is fard and the second is voluntary, which is also the position of Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad. If someone prays in a group and then finds another group, ash-Shafi'i says that he should not repeat the prayer with them. Ahmad says this only applies to Subh and 'Asr. Mālik says that if someone prays in a group, he should not repeat that prayer.

f: What are the positions of ash-Shafi'i, Ahmad, Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, and Mālik concerning an imam delaying his movement for someone joining the congregation and delegating another imam after losing wudu'?
b: The imam delaying movement and breaking wudu: If the imam senses someone joining while he is bowing or in the final tashahhud, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say it is recommended for him to wait. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik say that it is disliked. If the imam breaks wudu' it is recommended for him to delegate by Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Malik and Ahmad. Ash-Shafi'i has two statements, the soundest of which is that it is permitted to do so.

f: What are the positions of Mālik, ash-Shafi'i, Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, and Ahmad concerning the validity of following an imam when there is a road or river between the imam and followers, and when someone prays at home while following an imam in a mosque?
b: Connection of prayer rows to the imam: They agree that when the rows are connected and there is no road or river between them, following is valid. They disagree about what happens when there is a river or road between the imam and the followers. Malik and ash-Shafi'i say their prayer is still valid. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is not valid. If someone prays in his house with the imam's prayer in a mosque and there is a barrier which prevents him seeing the rows, Malik, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say their prayer is not valid, and in his best-known position, Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says the same.

f: What do the four schools say about following an imam who is performing a different type of prayer, particularly following a fard prayer with a nafl prayer and following one fard prayer with another?
b: Praying a prayer different to that of the imam: They agree that it is permitted for someone praying nāfila to follow someone praying a fard prayer. They disagree about the reverse. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Mālil and Ahmad say it is not valid and that it is not permitted to pray a fard behind someone praying a different fard. Ash-Shafi'i says it is permitted.

f: What are the positions of the four schools concerning praying behind a discerning child, a blind imam, an impious imam, and a woman leading men in obligatory or Tarāwīḥ prayer?
b: Valid and invalid imams: Praying behind a boy with discrimination in any prayer other than Jumu'a is absolutely valid in the view of ash-Shafi'i, who differs from the other three who say that it is not valid for a fard prayer and disagree about nāfila prayers. In the most likely report, ash-Shafi'i says that it is valid to follow such a boy in Jumu'a, but an adult has more right to be imam than a child. The imamate of a blind person is sound by agreement without any dislike, but Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that a seeing person is more entitled to be imam. The imamate of someone impious is valid in the view of Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ash-Shafi'i, who nevertheless disliked it. Mālik says that if an imam's impiety is not a matter of interpretation, his imamate is invalid and the prayer behind him should be repeated. There are two versions from Ahmad, the best known of which is that the prayer is not valid. It is agreed that it is not valid for a woman to lead a man in fard prayers. They disagree about whether a woman can act as imam for men in the tarāwīh prayer. Ahmad allows it provided she is behind, but the rest forbid it.

f: What are the positions of Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Mālik, ash-Shafi'i, and Ahmad concerning who is most entitled to lead the prayer, and the validity of an illiterate person leading someone who can recite the Fātiḥah?
b: Most entitled imam: They disagree about who is most entitled to be imam and whether it is the person with the most fiqh or the one who knows the most Qur'an. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Mālik and ash-Shafi'i say that the person with most fiqh is the most entitled, provided he can recite the Fatiha well. Ahmad says that the person with the most Qur'an, who is good in recitation and knows the rules of the prayer following is valid. They disagree about someone illiterate who does not know the Fatiha well leading someone who does. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that the prayer of both is invalid. Mālik and Ahmad say that the prayer of the reciter alone is invalid. Ash-Shafi'i says that it is valid for an illiterate to lead a group in prayer. There are two statements from him about what is the position of the prayer behind him of someone who can read, the soundest of which is that it is invalid.

f: What are the positions of the four schools concerning praying behind an imam who has broken wudu', especially when the imam or congregation is unaware of his impurity?
b: Impurity of the imam: It is not permitted to pray behind someone who has broken wudu'. If someone does not know it, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say that his prayer is valid, except in Jumu'a. In Jumu'a, if there are the required number of people without him, the prayer behind such a man is invalid in the school of ash-Shafi'i. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad say that the prayer behind someone who has broken wudu' is invalid in every case. Mālik says that if the imam has forgotten that, the prayer of those behind him is valid. If he knows, it is invalid.

f: What is the ruling on praying behind a seated imam according to Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, ash-Shafi'i, Malik, and Ahmad?
b: Praying behind a seated imam: The prayer of someone standing behind someone sitting is valid according to Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and ash-Shafi'i. Two things are reported from Malik. Ahmad says that people should pray behind him sitting.

f: What do Malik, ash-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ say about when the imam should stand and begin the prayer in relation to the iqama?
b: The imam and the iqama: Malik, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say that the imam must wait after the iqama until the rows are straight. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that when the mu'adhdhin says in the iqama, "Come to prayer," he stands and those behind him follow. When he says, "Qud qamat," the imam says the takbir al-ihram. When the iqama is over, the imam begins to recite.

f: How should men, boys, and women stand in the prayer rows according to the Shafi'ite position and Malik, and what happens if a woman stands in the first row or someone stands alone in a row?
b: Women and boys in the prayer: If boys are with the men, the Shafi'ite position is that the men should stand in one row and the boys behind them. Some of his people say that one boy should stand between every two men to teach them the prayer. That is the position of Malik. If there are women, they should stand behind the boys. If a woman stands in the first row between the men, the prayer of all of them is invalid. According to Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, the prayer of the man on her left, right and behind her is invalid, but her prayer is not. If someone stands in a row on his own, his prayer is allowed by three, but disliked. Ahmad says that his prayer is invalid if he is alone when the imam bows.

f: What is the ruling if a follower stands in front of the imam during the standing portion of the prayer?
b: Getting in front of the imam: If a follower is in front of the imam in the standing, his prayer is invalid according to Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad, while Malik says that it is valid. Ash-Shafi'i has two positions. The predominant one is that it is invalid.

f: What is the basic ruling on shortening prayers while travelling, and do the four schools regard shortening as an indulgence or a firm instruction?
b: The Travelling Prayer They agree that it is permitted to shorten the prayer while travelling, but they disagree whether it is an indulgence or a firm instruction. Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is a firm instruction and is strict about it. Malik, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say that it is an indulgence which is permitted while travelling. All but Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ say that it is not permitted to shorten the prayer on a journey which involves disobedience to Allah.

f: What minimum distance for shortening the prayer is attributed to the four schools, and what is the ruling on praying the full prayer after travelling three days?
b: Minimum distance for shortening: It is not permitted to shorten the prayer except for a distance of two days or a day and night, which is sixteen parsangs or four mail-stages in the view of ash-Shafi'i, Malik and Ahmad. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it should not be shortened for a journey of less than twenty-four parsangs. If someone travels a distance of three days, it is agreed that it is better to shorten but allowed to pray in full. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is not allowed to do the prayer in full and that is also the position of some Malikīs

f: At what point does a traveller become permitted to shorten the prayer according to Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, ash-Shafi'i, and the two reported positions of Malik?
b: The point where shortening begins: It is only permitted to shorten the prayer after leaving the houses of the town from which the journey starts according to Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and ash-Shafi'i. There are two versions from Malik. One is that he should leave them so that there are none level with him, and the second is that he should go three miles.

f: What is the ruling when a traveller prays behind a resident imam, and what happens if the traveller follows a resident in Jumu'a intending shortened Zuhr?
b: A traveller praying behind a resident: If a traveller follows a resident in any part of the prayer, he must do the full prayer except in the case of Malik who says that if someone catches a whole rak'at of the prayer of a resident, he must pray it in full, otherwise not. If someone prays Jumu'a and a traveller follows him intending a shortened Zuhr, he must do it in full because the Jumu'a prayer is the prayer of a resident. That is the position of ash-Shafi'i.

f: Can a sailor who continually travels with his family and property shorten the prayer, and what is the ruling for someone such as a drover who is continually travelling?
b: Continual travel: If a sailor travels in a ship with his family and property, ash-Shafi'i says that he can shorten and that is also the position of Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik. Ahmad says he should not. It is the same with a drover who travels all the time. Ahmad says he has no permission but the other three say that he can shorten and not fast.

f: Is it disliked for a traveller who shortens the prayer to perform voluntary prayers during the journey?
b: Nafila prayers on a journey: It is not disliked for someone who shortens to do nāfila during their journey.

f: How long may a traveller intend to stay in a place while retaining the ruling of a traveller according to Malik, ash-Shafi'i, Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, and Ahmad?
b: Maximum stay to remain a traveller: If a traveller intends to stay in a place for four days, he becomes a resident according to Malik and ash-Shafi'i. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that if someone intends to stay for fifteen days, he becomes resident. Ahmad says he is resident if he intends to stay for a period of more than twenty prayers.

f: How should missed prayers be made up when a person misses them while resident or while travelling and makes them up in a different status?
b: Travellers making up missed prayers: If someone misses a prayer at home, he must make it up on a journey as a full prayer. If he misses a prayer on a journey and makes it up at home, ash-Shafi'i has two positions, the soundest of which is that he does it in full which is also what Ahmad says. The other is that he does it shortened which is what both Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Mālik say.

f: Which schools permit combining Zuhr with 'Aṣr and Maghrib with 'Ishā' while travelling, and what is the Hanafi position?
b: Combining prayers on a journey: It is permitted by Malik, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad to combine Zuhr and 'Aṣr, and Maghrib and 'Ishā', when travelling, advancing or delaying them. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is not permitted to combine two prayers with the excuse of travelling.

f: Which schools permit combining prayers because of rain while resident, and which prayers may be combined according to the different schools?
b: Combining prayers while resident: It is permitted because of rain to combine Zuhr and 'Aṣr, advanced to the beginning of the time, according to ash-Shafi'i. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is not permitted at all. Malik and Ahmad say that Maghrib and 'Ishā' can be combined but not Zuhr and 'Aṣr, whether the rain is strong or weak, but this allowance is particular to those who pray in a group in a mosque reaching which involves going through the rain. It is not permitted to join prayers on account of sickness or fear in the apparent school of ash-Shafi'i. Ahmad says it is permitted. The later Shafi'ītes allow a choice.

f: What is the ruling on the continuation of the fear prayer after the death of the Prophet ﷺ, how many rak'ats does it contain for residents and travellers, and how is it performed by a resident imam according to the three Imams and Malik?
b: The Fear Prayer They agree that the fear prayer continued after the death of the Prophet ﷺ, although it is reported from al-Muzanī that it was abrogated and Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it was particular to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They agree that it contains four rak'ats while resident and two on a journey. When resident the imam prays two rak'ats with one group and two with the other group according to three Imams. Malik says that the fear prayer should not be prayed while resident but his adherents permit it.

f: What do the four schools say about praying during intense fighting, indicating rukū' and sujud, carrying weapons during the fear prayer, and repeating the prayer when an apparent enemy turns out not to be an enemy?
b: Prayer during intense fighting: They disagree about the prayer when fighting is intense. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that people should not pray in this state but delay the prayer until it is possible. Mālik, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say that they should not delay, but pray according to the situation and are allowed to pray however they can, on foot, mounted, facing qibla or not. They should indicate rukū' and sujud with their heads. Is it necessary to carry arms for the fear prayer or not? Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, ash-Shafi'i in one view, and Ahmad say that it is recommended but not obligatory. Malik, and ash-Shafi'i in another view, say that it is mandatory. If people see a crowd and think that it is the enemy and pray the fear prayer and then it becomes clear that it is not, only ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad, according to one position, say that they should repeat the prayer.

f: What is the status of the Jumu'a prayer, and for whom is it obligatory?
b: The Jumu'a prayer Scholars agree that the Jumu'a prayer is fard 'ayn and not a fard kifaya. It is obligatory for residents but not travellers. It is not obligatory for children, slaves, travellers or women.

f: Who must attend Jumu'a if they live outside a city where Jumu'a is not performed but can hear the call, and what is the ruling on Zuhr for someone unable to attend Jumu'a?
b: Place of obligation: Anyone outside a city in a place where the Jumu'a is not performed who hears the call must go to Jumu'a, according to Mālik, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that anyone living outside the city does not have to go to Jumu'a, even if he hears the call. He is like a traveller who comes to a city where Jumu'a is held; he can choose between it and praying Dhuhr. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that Zuhr in a group on Jumu'a is disliked for someone who cannot go to Jumu'a. Mālik, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say that it is not disliked.

f: What is the ruling on Jumu'a when the 'Id falls on the same day, according to ash-Shafi'i, Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, and Ahmad, for people of the city and people from villages?
b: Coincidence of Jumu'a and the 'Id: When the 'Id falls on the day of Jumu'a, ash-Shafi'ī says that the people of the city must still perform Jumu'a, but it is not obligatory for people from villages who are present. They can pray the 'Id and leave. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that Jumu'a is obligatory for the people of the town and Ahmad says that it is not obligatory for the people of the villages or the town. They should pray Zuhr.

f: What is the ruling on travelling after midday on Friday for someone who would normally be required to pray Jumu'a, and what is the ruling on selling after midday and after the second adhan?
b: Travelling and selling on the day of Jumu'a: If someone is one of the people who would normally pray Jumu'a and wants to travel after midday, he is not allowed to do so unless he can pray Jumu'a on the way or will be harmed by staying behind his companions. Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik say that he should go before midday. There are two positions from ash-Shafi'i, the soundest of which is that it is permitted, which is one position of Ahmad. Selling after midday is disliked and harām after the second adhan. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and ash-Shafi'i say that it is valid while Malik and Ahmad say that it is not.

f: What is the ruling on speaking during the Jumu'a khutba when the speech cannot be heard, and what do the schools say about speaking or listening when someone can hear the speech?
b: Talking during Jumu'a: They disagree about people speaking during the khutba when no one can hear it. Ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say it is permitted but recommend silence. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is not permitted to speak and Mālik says that silence is mandatory. They disagree about someone who can hear someone talking during the khutba. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Mālik and ash-Shafi'i in the old school say that it is haram for both speaker and listener, although Malik permitted speaking in order to set things right, such as telling newcomers not to step over people. In al-Umm, ash-Shafi'i says that it is not haram but disliked. The well-known position from Ahmad is that it is haram for the listener to reply, but not haram for the speaker.

f: In what places is Jumu'a valid according to ash-Shafi'i, Malik, and Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, and is Jumu'a valid if the people of a city perform it outside the city?
b: Places where Jumu'a is valid: Ash-Shafi'i says Jumu'a is only valid in places inhabited by those by whom the Jumu'a is held. Malik says the only places in which Jumu'a must be held are towns in which the houses are connected and where there is a mosque and market. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that Jumu'a is only valid in a city when there is a ruler who orders it. If the people of a city go outside the city and hold a Jumu'a, it is not valid according to three, while Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says it is valid if it is close to the city.

f: Is the ruler's permission required for Jumu'a according to the four schools?
b: Ruler's permission: It is recommended that Jumu'a should only be held with the permission of the ruler. If it is held without his permission, Malik, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say it is valid while Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it can only be held with the permission of the ruler.

f: How many people are necessary for Jumu'a according to the four schools, can slaves and travellers form the Jumu'a congregation, and what happens if some members of the congregation leave during the prayer?
b: Numbers necessary for Jumu'a: Jumu'a is only held when there are forty men present, according to ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says four. Malik says it can be with less than forty, although it is not mandatory for three or four. If forty travellers meet for Jumu'a it is not valid, although Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is sound if they are in a place where Jumu'a can be held. Can a Jumu'ah congregation be constituted of slaves and travellers? Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik say that it can and ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say that it cannot. If the imam says the takbir with a sufficient number and then they leave, Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that if he has prayed one rak'at with a prostration, Jumu'a is achieved. His companions say that if they leave after he has said the takbir al-ihrām, Jumu'a is achieved. Malik says if they leave after he has prayed a rak'at with both its prostrations, Jumu'a is achieved. Ash-Shafi'i has several statements, the soundest of which is that it is invalid and he should complete it as Zuhr, and Ahmad says the same.

f: What is the valid time for Jumu'a according to the four schools, and what happens if Jumu'a begins within its time but continues after the time of Zuhr ends?
b: Time of Jumu'a: All but Ahmad say that Jumu'a is only valid at the time of Zuhr. Ahmad says it is permitted before midday. If it starts in the time and then goes on until the time ends, it should be prayed as Zuhr in the view of ash-Shafi'i. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that the prayer is valid if it goes outside the time. Malik says that if Jumu'a is not prayed until the time of 'Aṣr, it can still be prayed as long as the sun has not yet set.

f: When does someone who arrives late to Jumu'a catch the Jumu'a prayer according to Malik, ash-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ?
b: Arriving late for Jumu'a: If someone catches a rak'at with the imam, he has caught Jumu'a. If less, he has not and should pray Zuhr with four rak'ats, according to Malik, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that he has caught it with anything.

f: What are the requirements for the two khutbas of Jumu'a according to ash-Shafi'i, Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, and Malik?
b: The khutbas: They agree that two khutbas are a precondition for it and they must come before the prayer. The school of ash-Shafi'i is that the khutbas must contain five things: praise of Allah, prayer on the Prophet ﷺ, command to taqwa, recitation of an ayat and application for the believers. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that that it is enough if the imam glorifies Allah, says the shahada, even "praise belongs to Allah," while his companions say that it must have the minimum of what is normally called a khutba. Two things are reported from Malik, one of which is that it is enough if he glorifies Allah or says the shahada, and the other is that it must be what is customarily called khutba.

f: Is standing obligatory when giving the Jumu'a khutba, is sitting between the two khutbas obligatory, and is ritual purity required for the khutbas?
b: Standing to give the khutba: The imam should stand for the khutba when he is able to do so. They disagree about whether it is obligatory. Malik and ash-Shafi'i say that it is mandatory. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad say that it is not obligatory. Ash-Shafi'i makes it obligatory to sit between the two khutbas. Purity is a precondition for both khutbas in the school of ash-Shafi'i. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Ahmad and Malik say that it is not a precondition.

f: What are the rulings concerning greeting people from the minbar, praying the greeting of the mosque while the imam is giving the khutba, and allowing someone other than the khaṭīb to lead Jumu'a?
b: Various matters concerning the imam: When the imam ascends the minbar, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say that he should greet those present. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik say that it is disliked for him to greet them because he greets them when he comes out to them and should not repeat the greeting again on the minbar. If someone enters while the imam is speaking, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say that he should pray the greeting of the mosque. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik say that it is disliked. They disagree about whether it is permitted for the prayer to be led by other than the khaṭīb. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says it is allowed with an excuse. Mālik says that only the khaṭīb may lead the prayer. There are two positions from ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad, the soundest being that it is permitted.

f: What is the recommended recitation in the Jumu'a prayer according to the sunna, and what does Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ say about specifying particular suras?
b: Recitation in the Jumu'a prayer: Part of the sunna is to recite Surat al-Jumu'a and al-Munāfiqūn or al-A'lā and al-Ghashiyya. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says nothing is specified.

f: What is the ruling and timing of ghusl for Jumu'a according to the four schools, and can one ghusl suffice for both janāba and Jumu'a?
b: Ghusl for Jumu'a: Ghusl for Jumu'a is sunna with all the fuqahā'. It is recommended that the ghusl should be done immediately before going out to it. It is permitted from Fajr with Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad. Malik says that ghusl is only sound if it is done immediately before going to the prayer. This is recommended for those who are resident. A single ghusl for both janāba and Jumu'a is allowed by all except Malik.

f: How many Jumu'a congregations may be held in one town according to ash-Shafi'i, Malik, Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, and Ahmad?
b: Single Jumu'a in a town: Even if a town is large, there should not be more than one Jumu'a there according to ash-Shafi'i and Malik. Malik says that if there are several mosques in the town, it should be held in the oldest of them. Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says nothing about that, but Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says if the city has two distinct districts, there can be two Jumu'as. If it has one, then only one. Ahmad says that if the city is large, like Baghdad, there can be two Jumu'as. If there is no need, then it is not permitted. Ash-Shafi'i says that more than one is permitted if the dimensions of a city make it necessary.

f: What should someone do if they miss the Jumu'a prayer, and may the missed Jumu'a be replaced by a congregational Zuhr prayer?
b: Missing Jumu'a: They agree that if someone misses Jumu'a, he should pray Dhuhr. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik say that he should pray individually and ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say that people may pray in a group.

f: What is the ruling of the four schools concerning the 'Id prayers?
b: 'Id prayers They agree that the 'Id prayers are prescribed and then they disagree. Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that they are an individual obligation like Jumu'a, while Malik and ash-Shafi'i say they are sunna as does one report from Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ. Ahmad says that they are a fard kifāya.

f: What are the preconditions for the 'Id prayers according to Ahmad, Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Malik, and ash-Shafi'i?
b: Preconditions for the 'Id prayers: They disagree about the preconditions for the 'Id prayers. Ahmad and Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ say that they include residency, number, and the permission of the ruler as is the case for Jumu'a. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ also says a city. Mālik and ash-Shafi'i say: none of these is a precondition. They permit it to be done individually by men and women.

f: How many additional takbīrs are performed in the 'Id prayers according to Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Malik, Ahmad, and ash-Shafi'i, and when are they performed relative to recitation?
b: Takbīrs for the 'Id prayers: They agree that it begins with the takbīr al-ihrām, but they disagree about the takbīrs after that. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that there are three in the first rak'at and three in the second. Malik and Ahmad say six in the first rak'at and five in the second. Ash-Shafi'i says seven in the first rak'at and five in the second. Ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say that dhikr is recommended between the takbīrs. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik say that the takbīrs should be continuous. They disagree about putting the takbīrs before the recitation. Mālik and ash-Shafi'i say that the takbīrs precede the recitation in both rak'ats. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that the recitation is consecutive so that the takbīrs in the first rak'at are before the recitation and in the second after the recitation. Ahmad has both statements. They agree about raising the hands in the takbīrs, although there is one transmission from Malik about raising them only for the takbīr al-ihrām.

f: What do the four schools say about making up the 'Id prayer when someone misses it with the imam, and how many rak'ats do Ahmad and ash-Shafi'i prescribe for the makeup?
b: Missing the 'Id prayer: They disagree about someone who misses the 'Id prayer with the imam. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik say that he should not make it up. Ahmad says that he should make it up alone. Both positions are recorded from ash-Shafi'ī, the soundest of which is that it should be made up alone. They disagree on how it is made up. Ahmad says that it should be prayed as four rak'ats like Zuhr and ash-Shafi'i says that it is made up with two rak'ats.

f: Where should the 'Id prayer be performed according to the schools, and when is it permissible to perform it in a mosque?
b: Place of the 'Id prayer: They agree that the sunna is to pray the 'Id prayer outside the city, not in the mosque, except for the Shafi'ites who say that it is better to pray it in the mosque if it is large enough. If it is held in the mosque for the frail Muslims, that is allowed.

f: What are the rulings of the four schools concerning nāfila prayers before and after the 'Id prayer, both at a prayer ground and in a mosque?
b: Nāfila prayers: They disagree about whether it is better to do nāfila prayers before or after the 'Id prayer. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that there are none before it but they can be prayed after it and that there is no difference between the imam and others in this respect. Malik says that if the prayer is at a prayer ground, there is no nāfila before or after for anyone. There are two positions if it takes place in a mosque. Ash-Shafi'i allows nāfila prayers before and after the 'Id prayer in a mosque, except for the imam. When he comes out to people, he should not pray before doing the 'Id prayer. Ahmad says that there is no nāfila before or after it. Shafi'i and Ahmad in another version say that he does. They say that it is not said after the nāfila except for ash-Shafi'i.

f: How should the 'Id prayer be announced, and which suras are recommended for recitation according to the four schools?
b: Call and recitation in the 'Id prayer: It is recommended that the prayer be announced with the words "The prayer is gathered" (Aṣ-ṣalātu jāmi'a.). Ash-Shafi'i says that Surat Qaf should be recited in the first rak'at and al-Qamar in the second, or al-A'la and al-Ghashiyya. Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that no sūra is specified. Malik and Ahmad say that he should recite al-A'la and al-Ghāshiyya.

f: What is the ruling when people discover after midday that the new moon was sighted and they had thought it was still the 30th of Ramadan, according to ash-Shafi'i, Malik, Ahmad, and Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ?
b: Uncertainty about the 'Id: If people arrive after midday thinking it is still the 30th Ramadan when the new moon has in fact been seen, the 'Id prayer should be made up according to the soundest position of ash-Shafi'i. Mālik says that it should not be made up. Ahmad says that if the people cannot be gathered on the day of the 'Id, then it is prayed the following morning. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that the Fiṭr prayer can be prayed on the second day and 'Adha on the second and third.

f: What are the positions of Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Ahmad, Malik, and ash-Shafi'i concerning the takbīrs on the Day of 'Arafa, the Day of Sacrifice, and the Days of Tashriq, and what is the ruling for someone praying alone?
b: Takbīrs on the days of 'Id: They disagree about the takbīrs at the 'Id of Sacrifice and Days of Tashriq and when it begins and ends in respect of the one in iḥrām and not in iḥrām. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad say that he says the takbīr from Fajr of 'Arafa until the 'Aṣr prayer on the Day of Sacrifice. Malik says from Zuhr of the Day of Sacrifice to Ṣubḥ on the last Day of Tashriq which is the fourth day of the 'Id. Ash-Shafi'i says what Mālik says, and in his school it is from Ṣubḥ of 'Arafa and ends with 'Aṣr of the last Day of Tashriq. They agree that the takbīr is sunna in groups. They disagree about someone who prays alone at these times. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad in one place say that someone praying alone does not say it. Malik

f: What is the form of the solar eclipse prayer according to the four schools, how is its recitation performed, and is a khutba prescribed?
b: The Eclipse Prayer They agree that the solar eclipse prayer is a confirmed sunna in a group and then they disagree about its form. Mālik, ash-Shafi'ī and Ahmad say that it consists of two rak'ats with two standings, recitations, rukū's and sujūds in each rak'at. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that they are two rak'ats like the Ṣubḥ prayer. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, ash-Shafi'i and Malik say that its recitation is silent. Ahmad says it is aloud. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad say that no khutba is sunna for the eclipse prayer. Ash-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Malik say that it is sunna for it to have two khutbas.

f: Is a congregational prayer prescribed for a lunar eclipse according to the four schools, and how is the recitation performed?
b: Lunar eclipses: Is a group prayer sunna for the lunar eclipse prayer? Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik say that it is not but it should be prayed individually. Ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say that it is sunna in a group as for the solar eclipse. Recitation is aloud. The eclipse prayer can be prayed individually as well as in a group.

f: What is the ruling on performing a special prayer for natural phenomena other than solar and lunar eclipses, such as earthquakes, lightning, or daytime darkness?
b: Prayer for other natural phenomena: There are other signs than the eclipse, such as earthquakes, lightning bolts and darkness in the day for which there is no prayer with the three, except for Ahmad who says that a group prayer is prayed for every sign.

f: What do the four schools say about the rain prayer, including whether its congregational prayer is Sunnah, whether it may be performed individually, and how it is recited?
b: The Rain Prayer They agree that asking for rain is sunna, but they disagree about whether the prayer is a sunna or not. Malik, ash-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and the two companions of Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ say that the group prayer is sunna. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that the prayer is not sunna, but that the imam should simply go out and make supplication. It is permitted when people pray alone. Ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad says that it is like the 'Id prayer and its recitation is aloud. Malik says that it is two rak'ats like other prayers and the recitation is aloud.

f: Is a khutba prescribed for the rain prayer, how many khutbas are there, and what does the imam begin with according to the different schools?
b: Khutba in the Rain prayer: Malik, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say that it is sunna to have khutbas and there should be two after the prayer. The imam begins with asking for forgiveness. Ahmad and Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ say that there is no khutba, but only supplication and asking for forgiveness.

f: What is the ruling on reversing the outer garment during the rain-prayer khutba, and what do the scholars agree regarding repeating the rain prayer and praying for relief from excessive rain?
b: Reversing the outer garment: It is recommended for the imam and the followers to reverse their outer garments in the second khutba except in the view of Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ who does not recommend that. Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says it is prescribed for the imam but not the followers. They agree that if there is no rain on the first day, they should repeat the prayer on a second and third day. They agree that when people are harmed by too much rain, the sunna is to perform a prayer to ask Allah to remove it.

f: What do scholars agree about remembering death, making a will, directing a dying person toward the qibla, and the expenses of preparing the deceased for burial?
b: Scholars agree that it is recommended to remember death often and for those with property to make a will when they are healthy, and it is strongly recommended for them to do so when they are ill. They agree that when death is near, a dying person should be turned towards qibla. They agree that the cost of preparing the body for burial should come from the capital of the deceased before any debts are paid.

f: What are the rulings of the four schools concerning washing the dead, the condition in which the body is washed, the preferred water, washing between spouses, and tayammum when only a non-maḥram of the opposite sex is present?
b: Washing the body: They agree that washing the dead is a fard kifāya. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik say that dead bodies should be washed naked with the private parts covered. Ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say that it is better to wash them in a shirt. Cold water is better unless it is very cold or there is a lot of dirt. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that heated water is always better. They agree that a wife can wash her husband and that it is permitted for a husband to wash his wife, except for Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ who says that it is not permitted. If a woman dies and only an unrelated man is with her, or a man dies and only an unrelated woman is with him, the school of Malik, Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, and the soundest position of ash-Shafi'i is that tayammum is done for them. There are two views from Ahmad: one is tayammum and the other is that the washer ties a rag around his hand, which is one view of ash-Shafi'i.

f: What is the recommended method of washing the dead according to the schools, including wudu', cleaning the nostrils, combing matted hair, and arranging a deceased woman's hair?
b: Method of washing: It is recommended for the washer to do wudu' for the corpse and use the siwāk on the teeth and to insert his fingers into the nostrils and wash them out. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ does not recommend that. If the beard is matted, it should be combed gently with a wide-toothed comb. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that that should not be done. When a woman is washed her hair is tied into three plaits behind her. Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it should be left as it is.

f: What do the schools say about opening the womb of a deceased pregnant woman when the child is still alive?
b: Death of pregnant women: If a pregnant woman dies with a living child still in her womb, the womb should opened according to Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and ash-Shafi'i. Ahmad says not. There are two versions from Mālik.

f: What do the schools say about washing and praying over a miscarried foetus according to its age and signs of life?
b: Miscarriages: They agree that if a miscarried foetus is under four months, it should not be washed or prayed over. If it is more than four months, Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that if there is a sneeze, movement, suckling which indicates life, it should be prayed over. Mālik says the same but does not mention movement. Ash-Shafi'i says in one view that it should be washed and there are two views about praying over it. Ahmad says that it should be washed and prayed over.

f: What are the various rulings concerning intention, bodily discharge after washing, grooming the deceased, achieving purity, the number of washes, and the use of lote leaves and camphor when washing the dead?
b: Various details concerning the washing: An intention on the part of the washer is not obligatory in the soundest position of the Shafi'ites. It is one of the positions of Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ. Malik says that it is obligatory. If something emerges from a dead body after it has been washed, only Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik and the soundest position of ash-Shafi'i say that it is obligatory to remove it. Ahmad says that the body must be washed again if it comes from the genitalia. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik say that it is disliked to pluck the armpits, shave the pubes or trim the moustache of a dead person. Ahmad says that there is no harm in doing that and ash-Shafi'i has two positions. They agree that it is obligatory in the washing to do what will bring about purity. The sunna is for it to be done an odd number of times and that there should be lote leaves and camphor in the water used for the last washing. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad say it is recommended for there to be some lote leaves in the water used for every washing. Mālik and ash-Shafi'i say only in the last one.

f: What are the rulings concerning the shrouding of the deceased, including its minimum, recommended number and color of shrouds, women's shrouds, who pays for the shroud, and the shroud of someone who dies in iḥrām?
b: Shrouding the body: It is mandatory by agreement for the body to be shrouded before paying debts and heirs. The minimum is a cloth which covers the body. Ash-Shafi'i, Mālik and Ahmad recommended for a man to be shrouded in three cloths. They all recommend white. Five cloths are recommended for a woman. Malik says that there is no specific definition of what is meant by shrouding but what is desired is to cover the body. Ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad dislike a woman to be shrouded in yellow, red or silk, but Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says it is not disliked if she has money. The shroud is paid for from her money according to Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Mālik and Ahmad. If she has no money Malik says her husband must provide it. If the husband is poor, it should be supplied by the public treasury. Ahmad says that a husband is not obliged to shroud his wife. Ash-Shafi'i says that it comes first from what is left and then from a relative. No perfume is put on someone who dies in iḥrām, nor stitched garments, and his head is not scented. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that iḥrām ends with death and that the body of someone who dies in iḥrām should be treated the same as any other.

f: What is the ruling on the funeral prayer, its timing, praying over the bier in the mosque, and wailing or calling out over the dead according to the schools?
b: The funeral prayer: The prayer over a dead person is a fard kifāya. The Mālikīs say that it is sunna. It is not disliked to do it at any time according to ash-Shafi'i. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad say that it is disliked to do it at the three times when prayer is disliked. Mālik says that it is disliked to do it at sunrise and sunset. It is permitted, without dislike, to pray over the bier in the mosque according to ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Mālik say it is disliked to do so. It is disliked to wail over the dead but Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is not disliked to call out over the dead.

f: Who is most entitled to lead the funeral prayer, and what are the positions of the schools concerning the ruler, relatives, an appointed imam, and a person designated by the deceased?
b: The imam for the funeral prayer: They disagree about the person most entitled to lead the prayer. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Mālik, Ahmad and ash-Shafi'i in the old school say the ruler is more entitled than a relative. Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is better when the ruler is not present for a relative to put forward the imam of the region. In his new school, ash-Shafi'i says that it should be a relative. If the dead person has left instructions for a specific man to pray over him, all but Ahmad say that he has no more right than the relatives. Mālik says that a son should precede a father, a brother is better than a grandfather, and that a son has more right than a husband. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is disliked to advance a son before a father.

f: What are the preconditions for the validity of the funeral prayer according to the source?
b: Preconditions for the funeral prayer: The preconditions for the validity of the funeral prayer include purity and covering the private parts.

f: Where does the imam stand in the funeral prayer according to the different schools?
b: Position of the imam: The Imam stands opposite the head of a man and the middle of a woman with ash-Shafi'i and the Ḥanafīs, although Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ himself says at the chest of the man and waist of the woman. Malik says at the chest of a man and the waist of a woman. Malik says at the chest of a man and the middle of a woman.

f: How is the funeral prayer performed according to the schools, including the number of takbirs, raising the hands, recitation of al-Fātiḥah, and the salāms?
b: Form of the funeral prayer: There are four takbirs in the funeral prayer. If there are more than four, the prayer is not invalid. If someone stands behind an imam who does more than four, he does not follow him in any additional ones, although Ahmad says he should follow up to seven. Ash-Shafi'i says that the hands should be raised in all the takbīrs level with the shoulders. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik say that the hands should only be raised for the first. Ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad consider the recitation of the Fatiha after the first takbir to be fard. Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik say that no Qur'an is recited. There are two salāms with three, one to the right with Ahmad.

f: What are the rulings concerning someone who misses part of the funeral prayer, including when the latecomer should say the takbir and how long after death the funeral prayer may be performed?
b: Missing the funeral prayer: If someone misses part of the prayer with the Imam, he should begin the prayer without waiting for a takbir in the view of ash-Shafi'i. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad say that he waits for the takbir of the imam and says it with him. Two things are related from Mālik. Positions vary regarding how long after death the funeral prayer may be said. One view is that it can be said up to a month, as Ahmad says. Another is that it is as long as the body has not decayed, and it is also said that there is no time limit.

f: What are the rulings concerning praying over an absent deceased person, burying at night, and praying over a partial body?
b: Various ancillary matters: It is valid to pray for an absent dead person according to ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik say that it is not valid. It is not disliked to bury someone at night. Ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say that if part of a body is found, it should be washed and prayed over. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik say that this only happens if most of the body is found.

f: What are the rulings of the schools concerning performing the funeral prayer for a suicide?
b: Suicides: They agree that a suicide should be prayed over but they disagree about whether the imam prays over him. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and ash-Shafi'i say that he does pray over him but Malik says that the imam should not pray over a suicide or someone killed for a hadd. Ahmad says that the imam should not pray over killers or suicides.

f: What are the rulings concerning the washing and funeral prayer of martyrs, people killed while fighting rebels, rebels killed in fighting, and those killed unjustly outside of war?
b: Martyrs and rebels and murder victims: If someone is martyred while in janāba, he should not be washed or prayed over according to Malik and that is also the soundest position of the Shafi'ites. Abu Ḥanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that he should be both washed and prayed over. Ahmad says that he should be washed but not prayed over. If someone is killed while fighting rebels, he is not a martyr and Malik's view and the most likely position of ash-Shafi'i is that he should be washed and prayed over. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that he should not be washed or prayed over. Two things are reported from Ahmad. If one of the rebels is killed in the fighting, he should be washed and prayed over, according to all but Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ. If someone is killed unjustly outside of war, he is washed and prayed over, according to Malik, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that if he is killed with iron, he is not washed, but if he is killed with a blunt instrument, he is washed and prayed over.

f: What do the schools agree about circumcising someone who dies uncircumcised?
b: No circumcision: They agree that if someone dies uncircumcised, he should not be circumcised. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Mālik and ash-Shafi'i in the old school say that it is not allowed and Malik says that the one who does it should be punished.

f: What are the preferred methods of carrying the bier and walking in relation to it according to the schools?
b: Carrying the bier: They agree that carrying the dead is a pious action. It is best that the body should be carried between two poles by four men according to ash-Shafi'i. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad say that four men is best. Mālik, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say it is best to walk in front of the bier. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says it is better to walk behind.

f: What should be done if someone dies at sea and the ship is not near the shore?
b: Death at sea: If someone dies at sea and the ship is not near the shore, it is best to put the body between two planks and cast it into the sea, if there are Muslims on the adjacent coast. If there are unbelievers, it should be weighted and thrown into the sea according to three. Ahmad says it is weighted in every case if burial is impossible.

f: When is it permissible to disinter a corpse after burial in order to bury another person?
b: Disinterment: When a corpse is buried, it is not permitted to disinter it to bury another, unless it has been such a time that the corpse is completely decayed and turned to dust.

f: What are the rulings concerning placing the deceased into the grave and the method of lowering the body into it according to the schools?
b: Placing in the grave: They agree that it is not recommended to bury someone in a coffin. The head of the corpse is placed at the end of the grave and then it is slid into the grave according to three of the Imams. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that the corpse is put on the edge of the grave towards the qibla and then brought down level.

f: What is the sunna concerning the shape of the grave, and what do the schools say about flattening or mounding the grave and entering it while wearing shoes?
b: Shape of the grave: The sunna is to flatten the grave when it is filled in. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Mālik and Ahmad say that mounding it is better because flattening is what the Shi'ites do. It is not disliked to get down into the grave wearing shoes with the other three, but Ahmad dislikes it.
