It is recommended to stone after sunrise. If someone stones after midday, that is permitted in the view of ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad. Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that stoning is only permitted after dawn. The talbiya ends when the Jamra al-'Aqaba is stoned according to three imams, while Malik says that it ends after midday on the day of 'Arafa.

f: What are the four actions of the Day of Sacrifice, what is their recommended or required order, and how much hair must be shaved?
b: The Day of Sacrifice: The actions of the Day of Sacrifice are four: stoning, sacrifice, shaving and tawāf. Three recommend that they be done in that order, but Ahmad says that the order is mandatory. It is best to shave the head. They disagree about the minimum of what is obligatory. Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says a quarter of the hair. Mālik says all or most. Ash-Shafi'i says three hairs are enough. If someone is bald, he should run the razor over his head. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that doing that is not recommended.

f: What are the rulings concerning the sacrifice in hajj, including marking and garlanding animals, ownership of voluntary and vowed sacrifices, drinking their milk, eating from sacrifices, sacrificing at night, and the preferred places for sacrifice?
b: Sacrifice: Sacrifice is recommended. It is recommended to mark the sacrificial animals, if they are camels or cattle, on the right side of the hump in the view of ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad. Mālik says on the left side, while Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says it is unlawful to mark them at all. It is recommended to garland camels with sandals and all except Ahmad say that this is done with sheep as well. He says that it is not recommended to garland sheep. When a person's sacrifice is voluntary, the animal remains his property until he slaughters it. If it is on account of a vow, he does not own it, the poor do, and he cannot sell or exchange it according to all but Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, who says that he can sell and exchange it. He can drink its extra milk although Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that that is not permitted. He cannot eat any animal he is obliged to sacrifice as expiation. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that he can eat the sacrifices of qirān and tamattu', and Malik says he can eat from all of them, except those sacrificed in expiation for hunting and as fidya for injury. Sacrificing at night is disliked and Malik says that it is not permitted. The best place to sacrifice is Marwa for 'umra and Mina for hajj. Mālik says that someone doing 'umra may only slaughter at Marwa and someone doing hajj only at Mina.

f: What is the status and timing of Tawaf al-Ifāda, and what is the consequence according to Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ of delaying it until the third day?
b: Tawaf al-Ifada: Tawaf al-Ifāda is a pillar of the hajj by agreement. The beginning of its time is the middle of the night before the Day of Sacrifice. The best time is midday on the Day of Sacrifice. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that its time begins at dawn on the Day of Sacrifice and ends on the second of the Days of Tashriq. If anyone delays it to the third day, he owes a sacrifice.

f: What are the obligatory rulings for stoning the three jamras during the Days of Tashriq, including their timing, number of pebbles, order, and the Hanafi ruling if the order is reversed?
b: Stoning the jamras: One of the obligatory parts of hajj is to stone the three jamras in the Days of Tashriq after midday, with seven pebbles each. The first to be stoned is the one closest to the Khayf mosque, then the middle one and then the Jamra al-'Aqaba. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that if someone reverses the order, he should repeat the stoning but that if he does not do so, he does not owe any sacrifice.

f: What are the “numbered days” and the “known days” mentioned in the Qur'an according to the different schools?
b: The "numbered days": The "numbered days" mentioned in the Qur'an are the Days of Tashriq and "the known ones" are the first ten days of Dhū'l-Hijja, according to ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad. Malik says that they are three of the Days of Sacrifice and the two days after them. Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that they are the Day of 'Arafa and first of the Days of Tashriq.

f: What is the ruling on the Farewell Tawaf, and what exception and Hanafi qualification are mentioned?
b: The Farewell Tawaf: The Farewell Tawaf is one of the obligatory parts of hajj, according to the well-known position of the fuqahā' except for someone who stays. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is not cancelled by staying.

f: What should a pilgrim do if an enemy prevents him from reaching 'Arafa, tawaf, or sa'y but another route is available, and what should he do if taking that route causes him to miss hajj or if no alternative route exists?
b: By an enemy: If someone is obstructed by an enemy from standing on 'Arafa, tawaf or sa'y but there is another route by which he can reach them, he must take it, whether it is near or far, and he should not come out of ihram. If he takes it and by doing so misses hajj, or if there is no other alternative route, he should come out of ihrām after 'umra.

f: What are the different rulings concerning a pilgrim who is prevented by illness from completing hajj or 'umra and whether a prior stipulation allows him to leave ihram?
b: By illness: If someone is prevented by illness, then the most likely school of ash-Shafi'i is that if he stipulated he could leave ihram, then he can. Mālik and Ahmad say that he cannot leave it because of illness, and Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that he can absolutely.

f: Can a woman assume ihram for hajj without her husband's permission, and can a husband require his wife to leave ihram?
b: Is a husband's permission needed: A woman can assume ihrām for hajj without her husband's permission in the view of Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Malik and Ahmad. The position of ash-Shafi'i varies about this, and the most likely is that he forbids it. Can the husband make his wife come out of ihram? There are two statements from ash-Shafi'i, the more evident is that he can. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik say that he cannot.

f: What is the ruling on sacrifice by people who are not performing hajj, including whether it is sunna or obligatory, the role of the zakat niṣāb, its starting and ending times, and what happens if a mandatory sacrifice is delayed beyond the Days of Tashriq?
b: It is prescribed in the Shari'a by agreement. They disagree about whether it is sunna or obligatory. Malik, ash-Shafi'i, Ahmad and the Hanafis say that it is a confirmed sunna. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is obligatory for those resident in cities. The niṣāb of zakat is considered when determining if it is obligatory. Ash-Shafi'i says that its time is after sunrise on the Day of Sacrifice when there has been enough time for the 'Īd prayer and two khutbas, whether the Imam has prayed it or not. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Malik and Ahmad say that one of the preconditions for the validity of sacrifices is that the imam has prayed and given the khutba, but Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is permitted for people in an agricultural region to sacrifice at the second dawn (i.e. the time of Fajr). Ash-Shafi'i says that the end of its time is sunset on the last of the Days of Tashriq. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Mālik say that it ends on the second of the Days of Tashriq. If the sacrifice is mandatory, the sacrifice is not cancelled when the Days of Tashriq end. A sacrifice must still be made according to all the Imams except Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, who says that it is cancelled.

f: What are the rulings concerning cutting hair and trimming nails during the first ten days of Dhū'l-Hijja for someone intending to sacrifice, according to the four schools?
b: Leaving hair and nails: When the first ten days of Dhū'l-Hijja have begun and someone intends to sacrifice, Malik and Ash-Shafi'i recommend that he should not have his hair cut or trim his nails until he has sacrificed. If he does, that is disliked. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is permitted and neither recommended or disliked while Ahmad says it is unlawful.

f: What defects and conditions affect whether an animal is acceptable for sacrifice, including illness, blindness, broken horns, lameness, and missing parts of the ear or tail?
b: Acceptable animals: When someone is restricted to a particular animal to sacrifice and the animal is healthy, but then a defect befalls it, that does not prevent its acceptability according to all but Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, who says it does. An animal which is slightly ill is allowed. A major illness which affects the meat, or mange which is evident, precludes it being acceptable for sacrifice. No blind or one-eyed animal is acceptable. An animal with a broken horn is disliked, and Ahmad says that it is not acceptable. Malik and ash-Shafi'i say that lame animals are not acceptable, but Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that they are. The Imams are agreed that an animal with part of its ear cut off is not acceptable, nor is one with the tail cut off because some meat is missing. If a slight amount is cut, then the most likely position of the Shafi'i school is that it is forbidden. Later Shafi'ites say that it is all right. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik says that if the minimum is missing, it is allowed, but if it is a lot, it is not. Ahmad says more than a third.

f: What are the rulings concerning delegating someone else to slaughter a sacrifice, including whether a dhimmi may be appointed?
b: Delegation: It is permitted to delegate someone else to slaughter, even a dhimmi, although it is disliked by three of the Imams. Mālik says that it is not permitted to delegate a dhimmi.

f: What are the rulings concerning mentioning Allah when slaughtering a sacrifice, including deliberate omission, forgetfulness, and saying a prayer on the Prophet ﷺ?
b: Mentioning Allah: It is recommended to mention Allah in the sacrifice and other things. If someone omits to do that, Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that if it is deliberate, the sacrifice may not be eaten. If he forgets, it may be eaten. Mālik says that if it is deliberate, it is not permitted, and if it is out of forgetfulness, there are two views. A third view is that it is absolutely lawful, whether it is deliberate or due to forgetfulness. Ash-Shafi'i says that if someone forgets, it does not matter. Ahmad says that it may not be eaten if it is deliberate, and there are two positions if it is out of forgetfulness. Ash-Shafi'i recommends saying the prayer on the Prophet ﷺ when slaughtering. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik say that doing so is disliked. Ahmad says that no particular formula is prescribed, but that the words, "O Allah, this is from You and to You, so accept it from me" may be used.

f: What are the rulings concerning eating from a sacrificial animal, distributing its meat, sacrifices made because of vows, and selling the sacrifice or its skin?
b: Eating the meat: If the sacrifice is voluntary, it is recommended to eat some of it. Some say it is mandatory. Ash-Shafi'ī says it is best to eat a third, give away a third as gifts and give a third as charity. If it is on account of a vow, none of it may be eaten by the person who has made the vow. It is not permitted to sell any sacrifice, whether from a vow or on a voluntary basis, nor to sell the skin.

f: Which animals are considered best for sacrifice, how many people may share a camel or cow, and what does Mālik say about sharing a voluntary sacrifice?
b: Best animals to sacrifice: Camels are the best animals to sacrifice, then cattle, then sheep. Malik says that sheep are best, then cattle, then camels. A camel fulfils the duty for seven people, and a cow and sheep for one. Seven can share in a camel, whether they are from separate or the same households. Mālik says that if it is voluntary and they are from the same household, it is permitted.

f: What is the ruling on the ʿaqīqa, how many animals are sacrificed for a boy and girl, and when should it be performed?
b: 'Aqiqa: The 'aqiqa is sunna according to Malik and ash-Shafi'i. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is permitted but not a recommended sunna. Ahmad has two statements, the best known of which is that it is sunna and the second that it is mandatory. It consists of two sheep for a boy and one for a girl. Malik says that there is one for a boy and one for a girl. It should be done on the seventh day after the birth of the child.

f: What is a vow, what is its ruling when it concerns an act of disobedience, and what are the rulings for vows to slaughter one's son or kill oneself?
b: A vow is a promise to carry out an act of devotion and it is binding. If it is a vow to perform an act of disobedience, it is not permitted to carry it out, and they disagree about whether kaffāra is obliged for it. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Mālik and ash-Shafi'i say that there is no kaffāra for not fulfilling the vow. Ahmad has two statements, one is that the vow is binding but one is not permitted to do it and so there must be kaffāra. To vow something unlawful is not valid, like fasting the 'Īd or fasting when menstruating. If someone vows to slaughter his son, nothing is binding on him with ash-Shafi'i. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik say that he is obliged to slaughter a sheep. Ahmad has two versions, one is that he must slaughter a sheep and the other that he must expiate the oath. If he vows to kill himself, three say that nothing is obliged of him, and Ahmad has two reports, one being that he should slaughter a ram, and the second that he should expiate the oath.

f: What is the ruling on a general or unspecified vow, and what must someone do if he makes such a vow but does not fulfill it?
b: General vows: If someone makes a general vow, it is valid in the view of Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Malik and Ahmad, and if he does not fulfil it, he owes the expiation of an oath for it. Ash-Shafi'i has two positions, one like that of the rest, and the second that it is not valid unless it is actually connected to something.

f: What are the rulings when someone makes a vow to perform an act of devotion conditionally as part of an argument, such as promising a fast or charity if he speaks to someone?
b: Vows in an argument: If someone vows an act of devotion by way of argument, like saying, "If I speak to so-and-so, then I owe Allah a fast or ṣadaqa", the most likely position in the school of ash-Shafi'i is that he can choose between expiation of the oath and doing what he said. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that he must do what he said in every case and he is not permitted to expiate it, and the other position is that there is kaffāra. Mālik says that he can expiate and also says that he should do what he has vowed.

f: What are the rulings concerning a vow to perform hajj, including whether it must be fulfilled or whether kaffāra may substitute for it?
b: Vowing to perform hajj: If someone vows to perform hajj, he must carry out the vow and nothing else is permitted, in the view of Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik, but ash-Shafi'i has two statements, one of them is that it must be fulfilled, which is the sounder, and the second is that he can choose between fulfilling it and expiating the oath. Ahmad has two statements.

f: What must someone do if he vows to give all or part of his wealth as ṣadaqa, according to the different schools?
b: Vowing to give away one's wealth: If someone vows to give away his money as ṣadaqa, ash-Shafi'i says that he must give away all his wealth. The Hanafis say that it is recommended to give away a third of all his zakatable wealth, and they have another statement that he should give it all away. Mālik says that he should give away a third of all his wealth. Ahmad has two statements: one is that he gives away a third, and the other is that it refers to the property which he meant.

f: What is the ruling on a vow to pray in the Masjid al-Ḥarām, and does the same ruling apply to the Mosque of Madina and al-Aqsa Mosque?
b: Vowing to pray in the Masjid al-Ḥarām: If someone vows to pray in the Masjid al-Ḥarām, he must do it. The same holds true for the Madina Mosque and al-Aqsa Mosque according to Malik and Ahmad, and that is the soundest position of ash-Shafi'i. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that someone cannot make a vow to pray in a particular mosque.

f: What are the rulings when someone vows to fast a certain day and then breaks the vow for a valid reason, and how may a vow to fast ten days be fulfilled?
b: Vowing to fast a certain day: When someone vows to fast a certain day and breaks his vow for a reason, he must make it up with three, but Malik says that if he breaks it on account of illness, he does not have to make it up. If he vows to fast ten days, he can fast them continuously or separately.

f: What are the rulings concerning a vow to go to the Masjid al-Ḥarām without intending hajj or 'umra, a vow to walk there, and vows to walk to Madina or al-Aqsa Mosque?
b: Vowing to go to the Masjid al-Ḥarām: If someone vows to go to the Masjid al-Ḥarām, but has no intention for hajj or 'umra or vows to walk there, then the famous position of Malik and Ahmad is that he is obliged to intend it as hajj or 'umra and that he must walk from his home. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that he does not have to walk unless he vowed to walk. Ash-Shafi'i has two statements about a vow to walk to Madina or al-Aqsa, the soundest being that it is not binding, as Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ also says. The second is that it is binding, as Malik and Ahmad say.

f: What are the rulings concerning a vow to perform something that is ordinarily permissible, such as walking home, riding a horse, or putting on clothes?
b: Vowing a permissible action: If someone vows to do something merely permissible, like, "By Allah, I will walk to my house" or "ride my horse" or "put on my clothes", he owes nothing with Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik. Ash-Shafi'i says that if he does something other than what he stated, he owes the kaffāra of an oath, even if he is not obliged to do such an action. Ahmad says that the oath is binding and he has a choice between doing it and kaffāra.

f: What are the rulings concerning eating horse meat and the meat of mules and domestic donkeys according to the different schools?
b: Horses: Horses are lawful to eat for the Shafi'is, Ahmad, and the later Hanafis. Mālik says that horse meat is disliked and in the more likely position actually unlawful. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says it is unlawful. The flesh of mules and domestic donkeys is unlawful according to three Imams, while there is disagreement from Malik about that, it being reported that it is either strongly disliked or forbidden.

f: Which birds are unlawful to eat because they have talons or eat carrion, which birds are permitted, and what are the rulings concerning birds that are forbidden to kill?
b: Birds: Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad agree that all birds with talons which attack others, like falcons, hawks and eagles, are unlawful to eat, as well as those without talons which eat corpses, such as vultures and crows. Malik allows them absolutely. Other birds are allowed. It is famous that there is no dislike of eating those it is forbidden to kill, like swifts, hoopoes, bats, owls and peacocks, except for ash-Shafi'i who considers them unlawful.

f: What are the rulings concerning eating predatory mammals with claws, rabbits, giraffes, foxes, hyenas, rock badgers, and jerboas according to the different schools?
b: Animals with claws etc.: They agree that animals with claws which hunt, like lions, leopards, lynxes, wolves, cats and elephants are unlawful to eat with the exception of Malik. He allowed such meat but considered it disliked. Rabbits are lawful. Varying things are said about giraffes. Foxes and hyenas are lawful with ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad, but disliked according to Malik. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says they are unlawful. Rock badgers and jerboas are lawful in the view of Mālik and ash-Shafi'ī whereas Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says they are unlawful.

f: What are the rulings concerning eating small creeping creatures, locusts, hedgehogs, moles, snakes, weasels, and wildcats?
b: Other animals: Eating small creeping ground creatures like mice is forbidden by three Imams, while Mālik says it is disliked. Locusts, however, can be eaten dead in any case, but Malik says that any which have died without any discernible reason should not be eaten. Hedgehogs are lawful in the view of Malik and ash-Shafi'i, while Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad say that they are unlawful. Mālik says that there is no harm in eating moles and snakes when they are slaughtered. They disagree about weasels. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad say they are unlawful, and that is the soundest position of ash-Shafi'i. Malik says that they are disliked. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ considered wildcats unlawful, which is the soundest position of ash-Shafi'ī. Mālik says their meat is disliked. There are two positions from Ahmad: permitted and unlawful.

f: What aquatic animals may be eaten according to the four schools, and what are the different rulings concerning fish, shellfish, crabs, frogs, otters, dolphins, crocodiles, and other aquatic creatures?
b: Fish: Fish are lawful by agreement. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that the only aquatic creatures which may be eaten are fish. Mālik says fish and other things, including shell fish, crabs, frogs, otters and dolphins but he dislikes eating dolphins. Ahmad says that everything that lives in water may be eaten except crocodiles, frogs, and swordfish, but anything other than fish must be properly slaughtered. The Shafi'ites disagree: some allow every aquatic creature, which is the soundest position, but some say only fish, and some exclude otters, dolphins, snakes and the like which resemble land creatures and may not be eaten.

f: What are the rulings concerning animals that eat impurities (jalāla), including eating their meat, milk, and eggs and how they become lawful again?
b: Animals which eat impurities (jalāla): It is disliked by three Imams to eat camels, sheep or chickens which eat dung (jalāla) and Ahmad says that their flesh, milk and eggs are unlawful. If they are kept and fed with pure food until the smell goes, they become lawful. It is said that that means forty days for camels and cattle, seven days for sheep and three days for chickens.

f: What are the rulings concerning eating carrion in a case of extreme hunger, including how much may be eaten and whether one should eat carrion or another person's food?
b: Carrion: If someone is forced by hunger to eat carrion he may do so. Ash-Shafi'i has two positions about eating it, the soundest being that it is mandatory. May someone eat their fill or only enough to survive? Ash-Shafi'i has two positions, one being that he should not eat his fill, which is the school of Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, and the second is that he should, which is the position of Malik and one view from Ahmad. The most likely position of ash-Shafi'i is that if lawful food is near, he is only allowed enough carrion to ensure survival, but if someone is completely cut off from permitted food, he may eat his fill and take provision from it. If someone is forced to choose between carrion and food belonging to someone else when the owner is absent, Malik, most of the Shafi'ites and some Hanafis say that he should eat the food of that person and that he is liable to pay for it. Ahmad and some Hanafis and Shafi'īs say that he should eat the carrion.

f: What is the ruling concerning fat or oil in which an animal such as a mouse dies, and can an impure liquid be purified according to the soundest Shafi'i position?
b: Fat in which an animal dies: In the case of fats like ghee and oil, when a mouse dies in it, if the substance is solid, then what the mouse has touched is discarded and the rest is pure and can be eaten. If it is liquid, it is all impure. Can an impure liquid be purified? The soundest position according to ash-Shafi'i is that it is impossible to purify it.

f: What is the ruling on the fat that Allah forbade to the Jews, and how do the different schools classify its consumption by Muslims?
b: Fat forbidden to the Jews: They disagree about the fat which Allah has forbidden to the Jews when they slaughter and whether it is disliked for Muslims or not. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and ash-Shafi'i say that it is permitted. Two things are reported from Malik: one is dislike and the other prohibition. Ahmad has two statements as well.

f: What are the rulings concerning drinking wine when someone is forced to do so because of thirst or for medicine?
b: Wine: As for someone who is forced to drink wine due to thirst or for medicine, Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says he may and ash-Shafi'i has three views about the matter, the soundest of which is that it is forbidden, the second that it is permitted, and the third permits it for thirst but not for medicine.

f: What are the rulings concerning eating ripe fruit from another person's unwalled garden without permission, including the case of necessity and the different positions of Ahmad?
b: Eating from someone else's property: If someone passes by someone else's garden, which does not have a wall, where there is ripe fruit, Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Mālik and ash-Shafi'i say that it is not permitted to eat without the permission of the owner, except in extreme need. If there is such need, someone may eat but is liable to pay for it. There are two positions from Ahmad, one being that it is permitted to eat without necessity and without liability, and the other that it is permitted in necessity and there is no liability. If there is a wall, the consensus is that it is not permitted to eat from it, except with the owner's permission.

f: What is the ruling on hospitality when a Muslim traveler asks for it from a Muslim resident of a village without a market, and how long does the obligation last according to Ahmad?
b: Hospitality: If a Muslim asks for hospitality from a Muslim inhabitant of a village without a market and he has no need, it is not obligatory to give him hospitality but it is recommended, according to three Imams, while Ahmad says that it is mandatory. He considers the period of the obligation to be a night, but three nights are recommended. If he refuses, Ahmad says that it becomes a debt for him.

f: What are the requirements for valid slaughtering according to the four Imams, including who may slaughter, which tools may be used, and which parts of the animal must be severed?
b: All four Imams agree that slaughtering should be done by a sane Muslim, male or female, who can do it well. They agree that slaughtering done by unbelievers other than the People of the Book is unlawful. They agree that slaughtering is valid with anything that makes blood flow and can be with a knife, sword, glass, stone or anything which has a sharp edge. Slaughtering involves cutting the windpipe and gullet. The arteries are not obligatory, in the view of ash-Shafi'i, although severing them is recommended by him and Ahmad. Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that the windpipe, gullet and one artery must be cut, while Malik says all four must be cut.

f: What is the ruling if an animal's head is completely cut off during slaughter, if it is slaughtered from the back of the neck, and how is life established before the required incision is made?
b: Cutting the head off: If the head is completely cut off, the animal is not unlawful. If an animal is slaughtered from the back of the neck and has not died before the windpipe is cut, it is lawful. If the animal has died before the windpipe is cut, it is not lawful in the view of Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and ash-Shafi'i. Life is noted by strong movement combined with bleeding. Malik and Ahmad say that it is not lawful at all.

f: What is the recommended position for camels, cattle, and sheep during slaughter, and what is the ruling if an animal is slaughtered in a different position?
b: Position of animals during slaughter: The sunna is to slaughter camels hobbled, while cattle and sheep should be slaughtered lying down. If a cow or sheep is killed like a camel or a camel is slaughtered like a cow, it is lawful with Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad, although it is disliked by Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ. Mālik says that if this is done without it being necessary, it should not be eaten. Some Malikis say that it is disliked.

f: What is the ruling when a pregnant animal is slaughtered and a dead fetus is found inside it?
b: Slaughter of pregnant animals: If an animal is slaughtered and a dead foetus is found inside it, it can be eaten in the opinion of three but not in the opinion of Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ.

f: What are the rulings concerning hunting with trained animals such as dogs and birds, including the requirements for training?
b: Hunting with animals:They agree that it is permitted to hunt with trained animals like dogs, leopards, falcons, and eagles, except for black dogs according to Ahmad. Three make it a precondition that the animals refrain from eating the game they are sent after and come when called. Malik says that this is not a precondition. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad say that the training of an animal has to be on two occasions for the animal to be considered trained. Ash-Shafi'i says it is what is considered custom, and Malik does not take that into consideration.

f: What is the ruling on saying “Bismillah” when releasing a hunting animal, including deliberate omission and forgetfulness?
b: Saying "Bismillah":Saying "Bismillah" when releasing the animal for game is sunna with ash-Shafi'i. If someone omits it deliberately, it is not unlawful. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is a precondition. If he forgets it, it is lawful. If deliberate, it is not. Malik says that if it is deliberate, it is not lawful, and if forgotten, there are two positions. Ahmad has various statements. The most evident is that if someone omits it when shooting or releasing the animal, it is not lawful to eat it.

f: What are the rulings when a hunting dog wounds game without immediately killing it and the hunter reaches it alive but it dies before he can slaughter it, and what if the hunting animal kills it by its weight?
b: Game injured or killed by hunting animals:If a hunting dog wounds but does not kill the prey and the hunter reaches the game while it is still alive and it dies before he can slaughter it, Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is not lawful. If the animal kills the game with its weight, ash-Shafi'i has two positions, one being that it is lawful, which is the sounder, and the well-known position of Malik, and the other that it is not lawful, and that is what is preferred by the Hanbalis. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ has two positions, the more likely being that it is lawful.

f: What is the ruling when a trained hunting dog eats part of the game it has caught, and does the same ruling apply to hunting birds?
b: Game eaten by hunting animals:If a trained dog eats some of the game, Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is not lawful and anything it has caught before that should not be eaten. Malik says it is lawful. Ash-Shafi'i has two positions: one is that it is lawful and the second, which is more likely, that it is not. A hunting bird is like a dog according to three of the Imams, but Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that what the hunting bird eats from is not lawful.

f: What are the rulings when hunted game disappears after being shot or bitten by a hunting animal and is later found dead?
b: Game found dead after some time:If someone shoots game or releases a dog on the game and it bites it and then the game disappears and it is found dead and the bite is part of the cause of death, a group of Shafi'ites say that it may be eaten, but the sound view of the school is that it should not be eaten, which is the position of Ahmad. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that if someone follows game immediately after shooting and finds it dead, it is lawful. If he delays following it, it is not. Mālik says that if he finds it during that day it is lawful. Later it is not.

f: What are the various ancillary rulings concerning traps, domestic animals that become wild, game split by a shot, hunting dogs that do not stop when called, birds found dead after falling, and game that escapes?
b: Various ancillary matters:If traps are set up and an animal falls into one and dies, it is not lawful to eat. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that if there are weapons in the trap and it is killed by the edge of one, it is lawful. If a domestic animal becomes wild and the owner cannot catch it, Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say that it is slaughtered in the same way a wild animal is when he does catch it. If someone shoots game and it splits in two, both parts are lawful in the view of ash-Shafi'i and one of two views from Ahmad. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that if they are equal, they are both lawful. Malik says that if the piece with the head is smaller, the animal is not lawful. If it is bigger, it is lawful and the other is not. If someone looses a dog on game and calls it but it does not stop but continues and kills the game, ash-Shafi'i says that it is not lawful to eat it. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad say that it is, and there are two views from Malik. If he shoots a bird and it falls to the earth and he finds it dead, it is lawful. If the game escapes from his hand, he still can claim it according to three Imams, but Ahmad says that if it goes far in the wild he ceases to have any right to it.

f: What are the general rulings concerning the lawfulness of trade, the prohibition of usury, the validity of sales by sane adults, children, insane persons, and people acting under coercion?
b: There is consensus that trade is lawful and usury unlawful. The Imams agree that trade is valid for every sane adult person who has freedom of choice and disposal. The sale of the insane is not valid. They disagree about the sale of a child. Malik and ash-Shafi'i say that it is not valid. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad say that it is valid if he has discrimination. But Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ imposes a condition that there be prior permission from his guardian. Ahmad stipulates that there be permission from the guardian. Three Imams consider a forced sale invalid, while Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is valid.

f: What are the rulings concerning silent transactions (bayʿ al-muʿāṭāt), including whether they constitute a sale and whether offer and acceptance are required for small and large items?
b: Silent transactions:A silent transaction is not a sale in the predominant opinion of ash-Shafi'i, and the same is reported from Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad. Mālik says that it is a sale, and other Shafi'ites accepted that, and it is found in a transmission from Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad. Is offer and acceptance a precondition for small items? Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is not for either small or large items, and in another position only for large items, which Ahmad also says. Mālik says that it is not a precondition at all, and that everything which people consider a sale is a sale. Something small is like a loaf of bread.

f: What are the rulings concerning the option to cancel a sale after it has been concluded, including the period for which such an option may be stipulated?
b: Option to cancel a sale:When a sale has been firmed up, each of the parties have the option to cancel, provided they have not parted or have stipulated a cancellation period. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and ash-Shafi'i say that it is permitted to set a cancellation period of three days, and no more. Malik says that it is permitted to set it according to what is needed, which varies with different goods. Fruit which will not last more than a day cannot have a longer cancellation period. When the period of the option ends, choice ends and the sale is binding.

f: What are the rulings concerning exercising an option to cancel a sale when the other party is absent, and what happens when the sale contains an unspecified cancellation option?
b: Invoking an option to cancel a sale:Someone who has an option may cancel the sale in the presence of the seller and also in his absence, according to Malik, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it must be in his presence. When there is an unknown option in the sale, then both the condition and sale are invalid with Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and ash-Shafi'i. Mālik says such a sale is permitted and the option is by custom. Ahmad says that it is valid.

f: What happens to the cancellation option when the buyer or seller dies during the option period, and when does ownership transfer during a time-limited option?
b: Death during cancellation period: If buyer or seller die during the period of the option, it is transferred to his heir according to three Imams, but Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is cancelled. When there is an option with a time period, is ownership transferred to the buyer in that period? Ash-Shafi'i has various statements, one being that transfer of ownership occurs by the contract, as Ahmad says. A second position is that it is when the option ceases, which is the position of Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik, and the third, which is preferred, is that ownership is suspended until it is finalised.

f: What kinds of pure and impure items may be sold, including dogs, wine, dung, and impure oil, according to the four schools?
b: What is permitted and not permitted in sales: There is consensus that selling a pure item is valid, but does selling something impure in itself, such as dogs, wine and dung, constitute a valid sale? Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is valid to sell dogs and dung and that a Muslim may delegate a dhimmi to buy and sell wine. The Malikis disagree about selling dogs: some allow it, some dislike it, and some say it is permitted for certain uses. Ash-Shafi'ī and Ahmad say that it is not permitted to sell anything of that nature and that a dog has no value that should be compensated if it is killed. Can oil which is rendered impure be purified by washing? The most likely position in the Shafi'i school is that it cannot be purified and so it is not permitted to sell it, which is the position of Ahmad and Mālik. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is permitted to sell impure oil.

f: What are the different rulings concerning the sale or leasing of women's milk, houses in Makka, and silkworms?
b: Various transactions:A woman's milk is pure and can be sold according to ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad, but Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik say that it is not permitted. Ash-Shafi'i says that it is valid to sell houses in Makka, while Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik say that it is not valid. There are two statements from Ahmad, the soundest of which is that it is not valid to sell or let them. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik say that it is disliked to let them. Selling silkworms is valid according to all but Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, who says it is not valid.

f: What are the rulings concerning selling something that belongs to another person without first obtaining the owner's permission?
b: Owner's permission in trade: It is not valid to sell what one does not own without the permission of the owner, in the new school of ash-Shafi'i. In the old school, it is contingent on the assent of the owner. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is valid but dependent on the permission of the owner. Buying is not dependent on permission. Mālik says that all transactions are dependent on permission. Ahmad has two positions.

f: What are the rulings concerning selling an item before taking possession of it, and how is possession established for movable and immovable property?
b: Sales without full possession: Ash-Shafi'i and ash-Shaybani say that it is not valid for someone to sell something whose ownership is not established for him, such as selling something before taking possession of it, whether it is movable or immovable property. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is permitted to sell immovable property before taking possession. Malik says that it is not permitted to sell food before taking possession of it, but that it is permitted in respect of other things. Ahmad says that if the item can be measured, counted or weighed, it is not permitted to sell it before receiving it, but that it is permitted in other things. Possession of what can be physically handed over is by transfer, and in immovable things, such as real estate and orchards, it is by vacation.

f: What are the rulings concerning selling things that cannot reliably be delivered and selling an indeterminate item from a collection of similar items?
b: Sales of intangibles and unknown quantities: It is agreed that it is not permitted to sell what cannot be guaranteed to be handed over, such as birds in the air or fish in water. Three Imams say that it is not allowed to sell an indeterminate article, like one cloth in a pile of cloth lengths. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ allows it with a cancellation option.

f: What are the rulings concerning the sale of an absent or unseen item that has not been described?
b: Sales of unseen goods:It is not valid to sell an absent article which has not been described, according to Malik, and that is the most likely position of ash-Shafi'i. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is valid, but the buyer has the option to refuse when he sees it. Ahmad says the sale is valid.

f: What are the rulings concerning selling broad beans in their pods and wheat in its husk?
b: Beans in the pod and wheat in the husk: It is not permitted to sell broad-beans in the pod, according to all but Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ who says it is permitted. It is not valid to sell wheat in the husk in the soundest view of ash-Shafi'i, while Malik, Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad allow it.

f: What are the rulings concerning selling a heap, land, or a flock according to a specified price per unit of measurement or per animal?
b: Representative sales:If someone says, "I will sell you this heap, a dirham for every cafiz," that is valid with Malik, ash-Shafi'i, Ahmad, Abū Yūsuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and ash-Shaybānī. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says it is only valid for one cafiz of it. If he specifies a number of cafīzes, it is valid. If someone says, "I will sell you this land, every cubit for a dirham," or "this flock, every sheep for a dirham," it is valid. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says it is not valid.

f: What are the rulings concerning selling bees in their hives, milk in the udder, and wool on the backs of sheep?
b: Unquantified sales:Three Imams say that it is valid to sell bees, even in their hives if they have been inspected, but Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says it is not permitted. Three Imams say that it is not permitted to sell milk in the udder, but Malik says it is permitted for a known number of days if the amount of the milk is known. It is not permitted to sell wool on the back of sheep, according to ash-Shafi'i, Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad, but Mālik says it is permitted, provided it is shorn immediately.

f: What are the rulings concerning buying and selling copies of the Qur'an, including selling them to unbelievers?
b: Buying and selling Qur'ans: They agree that it is permitted to buy Qur'ans, but disagree about selling them. Three of the Imams permit it without dislike, but Ahmad dislikes it. It is not permitted to sell a Qur'an to an unbeliever, according to ash-Shafi'i and is one of two positions from Malik. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says it is valid. Ahmad says it is not valid.

f: What is the ruling concerning selling grapes to someone who will use them to make wine?
b: Selling grapes to winemakers: It is agreed that it is disliked to sell grapes to a winemaker. Ahmad says it is not valid.

f: What are the rulings concerning receiving payment for the use of a male animal for breeding?
b: Stud fees: Stud fees are unlawful and the price received for them is forbidden with three while Malik permits a recompense for the covering of the stud animal for a specified period of time.

f: What kinds of conditions attached to a sale are considered invalid because they conflict with the purpose of the sale?
b: Invalid conditions: If someone makes a sale with a condition which is incompatible with the aim of the sale - such as selling a slave on the condition that he cannot be sold or freed, a house provided that the buyer lives in it, or a cloth provided that it is made up into a garment - the sale is void with Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and ash-Shafi'i. Mālik says that if the condition involves a use that is insignificant, such as living in a house, it is permitted. Ahmad says that if it stipulates living in the house for a day or two, it is not invalid.

f: What is the status of goods obtained through an invalid sale, and what happens to improvements made to land purchased through such a sale?
b: Status of goods bought in invalid sales: If a buyer takes goods in an invalid sale, it is agreed by three of the Imams that he does not own them, whereas Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that if he has taken them with the permission of the seller after exchanging something of value for them, he owns them if the price has been paid. If someone plants in land purchased in an invalid sale or builds on it, when the seller takes the land back, he cannot uproot the plants or destroy the building without being liable for the loss. Three Imams state that he can pay the price of the improvements and then owns it, but Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that he cannot take the land back but is paid the value of the land.

f: What are the six commodities unanimously recognized in the classical discussion of usurious transactions?
b: There is consensus that there are six items subject to unlawful usurious transactions: gold and silver, wheat, barley, dates and salt.

f: What are the forbidden and permitted forms of exchange involving gold, silver, wheat, barley, dates, and salt, including equality, immediate possession, and differences between the schools?
b: Forbidden and permitted transactions: There is consensus that the Muslims agree that it is not permitted to sell gold for gold alone or silver for silver, whether minted, ore or jewellery, except in equal weight from hand to hand. None of it which is absent may be sold for something present. They agree that it is permitted to sell gold for silver and silver for gold in disparate amounts. They agree that it is not permitted to sell wheat for wheat, barley for barley, dates for dates, or salt for salt when there is an accepted measurement, except like for like, hand to hand. It is permitted to sell dates for salt and salt for dates in disparate amounts hand to hand. It is not permitted for buyer and seller to part before taking possession, except in the view of Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ. Three Imams do not permit the sale of jewellery for the same minted metal in disparate amounts, but Malik says it is permitted to sell for its value in coin. There can be no disparity before taking possession in selling food for food, according to ash-Shafi'i and Malik, although Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says it is permitted.

f: What aspects of usury apply to commodities other than gold, silver, food, and drink, and how do the schools classify different commodities and categories?
b: Usury in respect of other things: Certain aspects of what could be considered usury are not forbidden when dealing with things other than gold and silver, food and drink, namely delay in payment or delivery, disparity and separating before taking possession. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that delay is unlawful only where the same category is concerned. Malik says that it is not permitted to sell one animal for two of the same species. Every two things which have the same name and character are the same category. If they differ, they are two different categories. Mālik says wheat and barley are the same category. There are two positions by ash-Shafi'i about milk and meat, the soundest being that they are different categories, and that is the school of Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ. There is no usury in respect of iron, lead and the like with Malik and ash-Shafi'i because gold and silver constitute the medium of exchange. Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad, in one position, say that usury extends to iron, copper and the like.

f: What are the rulings concerning selling commodities subject to ribā by estimation rather than exact measurement?
b: Sale by estimation:Things in respect of which usury is forbidden cannot be sold some for others by estimation, except dates on the tree for dates on the ground. Malik says that in the desert it is permitted to sell a measure by estimation rather than by exact weight.

f: What is the ruling on exchanging ribā commodities of the same category when one side contains an additional item that creates a disparity in value?
b: Disparity in value of items subject to usury: According to Malik and ash-Shafi'i, things in respect of which usury is forbidden cannot be sold against one another when one of the two has something else with it which creates a disparity in value. So two varieties of the same category may not be sold when their value differs, like a mudd of good dates and some dirhams for another mudd of good dates, or like one sound dinar and an unsound one for two sound ones. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ allows all of that.

f: What are the rulings concerning exchanging dry produce for fresh produce and the specific concession of ʿarāyā?
b: Dry produce for fresh produce: It is not permitted to sell dry produce for fresh on the ground, like selling fresh dates for dry ones. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ alone permits it by measure. As for 'ariyyas, which is that a man sell the dates on the trees by estimation for what is on the ground, ash-Shafi'i allows it in respect of amounts of less than five wasqs, and says it is not confined to the poor, which is the position of Ahmad. But he stated in one of two positions that the fresh dates may be estimated and sold for their equivalent in dry dates. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that this not permitted at all. Malik says it is permitted in one specific situation, which is when a man is given the fruits of some trees in a garden which it is hard for him to get to and so he sells it by estimation for dry dates which he receives. 'Ariyyas can be sold in separate contracts if they are more than five wasqs. Ahmad says that more than one is not permitted.

f: What are the rulings concerning exchanges involving grain, flour, bread, and meat from the same animal?
b: Grain, flour and bread: It is not permitted to sell grain for flour milled from that grain, according to Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad in one of two transmissions, but Mālik says it is permitted to sell it by measure. Ahmad says in another transmission that it is permitted to sell it by weight. It is not permitted to sell wheat flour for other wheat flour in the view of ash-Shafi'i and Malik, but Ahmad says that it is permitted, as does Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, if it is of the same quality. It is not permitted to sell flour for bread made from the same flour. The Hanafis permit selling wheat for bread without equivalence. It is not permitted to sell bread for bread when one or both are fresh. It is not permitted to sell an animal for meat from the same animal, with three Imams, while Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ permits it.

f: What is included in the sale of a house, and what movable items are excluded according to the stated Hanafi position and Zafar's view?
b: Included in the sale of a house is the land accompanying it and every building on it, including the bath-house, but that does not include things which can be carried like a bucket, winch, or bed. It includes doors, shelves, and stairs. Zafar says that if there are tools and furniture in the house, they are included.

f: What is the ruling on selling a date palm with unpollinated or pollinated spadices attached?
b: Pollinated palms: If someone sells a date palm which has unpollinated spadices on it, they are included in the sale. If they have been pollinated, three Imams say they are not included, except for Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ.

f: What are the rulings of the four Imams concerning the sale of ripe and unripe fruit while it remains on the tree?
b: Ripe and unripe fruit on the tree: It is not permitted to sell fruit before it is ripe without stipulating immediate picking, in the view of Malik, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says it is valid, and he considers that it necessitates that the fruit be cut. It is always permissible to sell the fruit after it is ripe, according to ash-Shafi'i, Malik and Ahmad. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is not permitted to sell fruit after it is ripe with the stipulation that the fruit remain.

f: What are the rulings concerning partial exclusion from a sale of produce, branches, a garden's fruit, and parts of a sheep?
b: Partial sales: If someone sells a load of produce and excepts from it some mudds or șa's, it is not valid, nor can he except one of the branches of a tree in the view of Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad, although Malik says it is permitted to do so. If someone says, "I sell you the fruit of this garden less a quarter of it," it is agreed to be valid. It is not permitted to sell a sheep and exclude some of it, the skin or anything else, from the sale. Ahmad says that the head and trotters can be excluded, and Malik allows that on a journey but not while resident.

f: What are the rulings concerning selling animals left unmilked and returning goods because of a defect?
b: Such things involve deceiving the buyer by making him think that the animal has more milk than it actually has and they are unlawful. Is the option to cancel the purchase confirmed? All but Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ say yes. When it is affirmed that the buyer has the option to return it, the return does not require the consent and presence of the seller. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says if it happens before taking possession, it requires his presence, and afterwards requires his consent or a judgement. The return of goods because of a defect must be immediate with Malik and ash-Shafi'i, but not the other two.

f: What is the ruling when a seller or buyer proposes keeping defective goods in exchange for compensation?
b: Compensation agreements: If a seller says to a buyer, "Keep the object and take compensation for the defect," the buyer is not compelled to accept. If the buyer says it, the seller is not compelled to accept. If they agree, the sale is valid with Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Malik and some Shafi'īs. Ahmad says that the buyer can keep the goods and ask the seller for compensation, in which case the seller is compelled to pay it to him.

f: What is the ruling according to Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and ash-Shafiʿi when a defect is discovered after the price has been paid?
b: Discovery of a defect after completion of sale: If a defect is discovered in the goods after the price has been paid, the buyer does not have the option to cancel the sale with Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and ash-Shafi'i.

f: What happens to increases in goods that occur while they are in the buyer's possession when a sale is cancelled because of a defect?
b: Increase in sold goods after a cancelled sale: In the event of a cancelled sale, if the goods increase in a clear way, like by producing offspring or fruit, the buyer keeps the increase and returns the original item, according to ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad. Malik says that if the increase is in the form of offspring, it should be returned with the original animal. If it is fruit, the buyer may keep it and return the original. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that increase in the possession of the buyer always prevents its return on account of a defect.

f: What are the rulings when defective goods have decreased in value because of a new cause while in the buyer's possession?
b: Decrease in value of defective bought goods: If a buyer finds a defect in the goods whose value has been lessened while in his possession by a cause other than the original defect, such as sexual intercourse with a virgin or the cutting of a piece of cloth, there is no barrier to his return them, but they should be returned with compensation. The new defect does not prevent the goods being returned. If the new defect was the only way of discovering the original defect, for instance opening up a melon or cracking open an egg, Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says the return is prevented. Ash-Shafi'ī's position is that it may be returned. Malik and Ahmad, in one position, say that it may not be returned and no compensation is owed.

f: What are the rulings of the four Imams concerning reselling purchased goods before paying the original purchase price, and what is the ruling on a murābaḥa sale?
b: If someone buys goods, ash-Shafi'i says he can sell them for the original price, or more or less than it, before or after paying the original purchase price. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Mālik and Ahmad say that it is not permitted to buy something from a seller for less than the price he paid before he has paid for it. It is, however, agreed that it is permitted to sell with murābaha (a specified profit), that is when a seller makes clear the original price he paid for some goods he is selling and specifies an increment, saying, for example, "I will sell it to you for its original price plus one dirham in every ten".

f: What is najsh (bidding up), what is its ruling, and what is the ruling on a city-dweller buying from a newly arrived bedouin with goods that are generally needed?
b: Bidding up: Bidding up merchandise is unlawful. Bidding up something is to make a higher bid for something, not out of the desire to buy it, but simply to trick another person into paying more. If someone falls for that and buys, then the sale is valid, with three, but Malik says that it is invalid. It is unlawful for a city-dweller to buy from a bedouin when he arrives as a stranger with goods for which there is general need.

f: What is the ruling on a sale involving an unrefundable deposit (bayʿ al-ʿurbūn) according to the four Imams?
b: Unrefundable deposits: A sale with an unrefundable deposit is unlawful in the view of three: that is for someone to give a dirham towards the price of some goods which then becomes part of the price if he likes the goods but is otherwise forfeited. Ahmad says that there is no harm in it.

f: What are the rulings of the four Imams concerning an ʿīna sale, and when is a subsequent purchase by the original seller permitted?
b: 'Ina sales: Ash-Shafi'i permits but dislikes the 'īna sale, which is when someone sells goods to a buyer for a certain price on credit and then buys them back from him for cash at a lower price. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Mālik and Ahmad say that doing this is not permitted if there is any disparity in the price. If a buyer sells the goods to someone other than the seller and then the seller buys them after that, it is permitted.

f: What are the rulings concerning fixing prices, including the positions of Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, ash-Shāfiʿī, and Mālik and the effect of a ruler's compulsion?
b: Price fixing: Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and ash-Shafi'i say that it is forbidden to fix prices. Mālik says that this happens when one of the people of the market increases or lowers the price and he is told, "Either you sell by the price of the people of the market or you leave." If a ruler sets prices and a man sells his goods when he does not want to sell them for that price, it is by compulsion. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that the compulsion of a ruler prevents the validity of a sale.

f: What is the ruling on hoarding foodstuffs, and what constitutes hoarding?
b: Hoarding: Hoarding foodstuffs is agreed to be unlawful. Hoarding means to buy food when the price is high and to withhold it in order to increase the price even further.

f: What is the ruling on selling a debt for a debt?
b: Selling debts for debts: They agree that it is not permitted to sell a debt for a debt.

f: What are the rulings of Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, ash-Shāfiʿī, and Aḥmad concerning selling dogs and the value of dogs?
b: Selling dogs: The price of a dog is considered offensive and Mālik dislikes but allows it. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says it is allowed for beneficial use. Ash-Shafi'i says that it is not allowed at all and it has no value, which is what Ahmad also says.

f: How are disputes over the price of a sale resolved when neither party has proof, and what are the rulings when the sold goods have been destroyed or are held by an heir?
b: Disputes in a sale: If there is a dispute about a price and there is no proof one way or the other, the parties should swear oaths. The soundest position of ash-Shafi'i is that the seller swears first, but Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that the buyer should start. If the goods are destroyed and the parties disagree about the price, ash-Shafi'i says that they should swear and the sale is voided and the price returned if it can be assessed. If the goods are replaceable, then the buyer must bring a replacement. This is one of two views of Ahmad and one of Malik's. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that there are no oaths when goods are destroyed and that the word taken is that of the buyer. That is also related from Ahmad and Mālik. Ash-Shafi'i says that it is the word of the seller which should be taken. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that if the goods are in the possession of the seller's heir, both parties should swear oaths, and if they are in the possession of the heir of the buyer, his word is taken when accompanied by an oath.

f: How are disagreements over preconditions concerning credit terms, an option period, pledges, financial liability, or promises resolved according to the four Imams?
b: Financial disagreements: If the parties disagree about a precondition involving the length of a credit term or the length of an option to cancel a sale, the stipulation of a pledge or financial liability, or a promise, they swear oaths, according to ash-Shafi'i and Malik. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad say that they do not swear oaths about any precondition and a denial from either party should be accepted.

f: When buyer and seller disagree in a credit sale about which party must perform first, who is compelled to deliver the goods and who is compelled to pay according to the stated positions?
b: Disagreements in credit sales: If someone sells an item for a price on credit and the buyer and seller then disagree about the transaction, and the seller says he will not hand over the goods until they are paid for and the buyer says he will not pay until he receives the goods, there are several views from ash-Shafi'i, the soundest of which is that the seller is compelled to hand over the goods, and then the buyer is compelled to pay the price. There are other positions. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik say that the buyer is compelled first.

f: What are the rulings when goods bought in a sale are destroyed before the buyer takes possession, whether by natural disaster, a third party, the seller, or destruction of fruit on trees?
b: Destruction of bought goods before possession: If bought goods are destroyed before possession by a natural disaster, then Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and ash-Shafi'i say that the contract is nullified. Mālik and Ahmad say that if the goods are not things which can be measured, weighed or counted, the buyer is liable. If a third party destroys them, ash-Shafi'i has several views, the soundest of which is that the sale is void. The buyer can choose between having the goods replaced and paying, or voiding the deal, or making the third party pay. This is the position of Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad, and the preferred view of Malik. If the seller destroys them, it is considered the same as a natural disaster, according to all except Ahmad who says that the seller owes their price or must replace them. If the goods in question consist of fruit on trees which have been destroyed after the land has been vacated, Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is the liability of the buyer, which is the soundest position of ash-Shafi'i. Malik says that if less than a third is destroyed, it is the liability of the buyer. If it is more, it is that of the seller. Ahmad says that if it is destroyed by natural causes, it is the liability of the buyer; if it is stolen, it is that of the seller.

f: What are the conditions for the validity of a salam (advance sale), and what additional condition does Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ require concerning the place of delivery?
b: Buying in Advance (Salam) and Loans (Qirād): The imams agree that buying in advance is permitted and its validity depends on six conditions: that the category of goods is known, their quality is known, their amount is known, the term of payment is known, and the amount of money is known. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that the naming of the place of delivery if it is something heavy is a seventh condition. The others consider this binding but not a condition.

f: For which types of goods is advance payment (salam) permitted, and how do the Imams differ concerning countable goods that vary substantially in size and quality?
b: Goods for which advance payment is permitted: They agree that it is permitted for things which can be weighed and measured and described. It is permitted for numbered things which are not dissimilar, like nuts or eggs, except in one position from Ahmad. They disagree about counted things which can differ greatly from one another, like pomegranates or watermelons. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that advance payment is not permitted for such things, since neither measure nor quantity are an adequate gauge, but Ahmad says that it is absolutely permitted. Ash-Shafi'i says that it is permitted by weight. Two things are reported from Ahmad: the most famous that it is permitted by quantity. Ahmad says that anything generally reckoned by weight cannot be done by measure or vice versa.

f: What are the various rulings concerning the availability of goods for salam, rare precious stones, and partnership or resale at a discount in advance sales?
b: Various factors: An advance sale is permitted in respect of countable things by Malik, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad, when it is probable that they exist in the place concerned. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is not allowed unless they actually exist when the contract for delivery is made. It is not permitted in respect of rare precious stones, except by Malik. Partnership and resale with discount are allowed in respect of advance sales in the same way as in other sales, according to Mālik, but Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad forbid them.

f: What are the rulings concerning qard (loans), the duration of a loan, lending bread, and whether loans of fungible goods are measured by weight or number?
b: Informal loans: Loaning (qard) things is recommended and it takes effect immediately when someone requests it for however long he wishes. A date set for it is not binding, although Malik says that it is binding. Three of the Imams say it is permitted to lend bread, but Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says it is not permitted. Is it permitted by weight or number? There are two views from ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad.

f: Is it permissible for a lender to receive a gift, food, or other benefit from the borrower during the loan, and what exception is mentioned concerning customary practice?
b: Added elements: When a man makes a loan to another, is it permitted for the lender to benefit from any of the property of the recipient in the form of a gift or food to which he invites him, or is that not permitted - unless it is custom during the period of the loan? Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Mālik and Ahmad say that it is not permitted. Ash-Shafi'i says that if it is not a precondition, it is permitted.

f: What are the rulings concerning repayment before the agreed term, accepting part of a debt in money and part in goods, cancelling or extending part of a debt after its term, and Mālik's position on a creditor granting a term?
b: Abiding by original agreement: They agree that if someone owes a man a debt with a set term, the debtor is not allowed to pay some of it before the term and delay some of it to a later term. It is also not permitted for the creditor to take some of it before the term in money and some in goods. There is no harm when the term comes if the creditor takes some and cancels some of the debt or delays it to another time. If a man owes a debt to another through a sale or a loan, and he gives a term, Mālik says that the creditor cannot retract it and he is obliged to wait until the expiry of that term. He can increase the term, except in respect of fines for physical injury and loans according to Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ.

f: What are the rulings concerning collateral (rahn) regarding its validity, possession, jointly owned collateral, and the effect of the collateral leaving the pledgee's possession?
b: Collateral is permitted at home and on a journey by all. The contract of the collateral must be accepted, even if it is not taken, and it is permitted to compel the pledger to surrender his collateral. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say that one of the preconditions for the validity of collateral is taking possession of it and so it must be taken. Collateral made with something which is jointly owned is permitted, whether it is something divisible, like immovable property, or indivisible, like a slave. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is not valid. Ash-Shafi'i says that it is not a precondition that the pledge should remain with the pledgee, but it is a precondition with Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik. If the collateral leaves the possession of the pledgee in any way, the pledge becomes invalid, except in the view of Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ who says it is not invalidated if it becomes a deposit with the pledger.

f: What is the ruling on using one existing pledge as collateral for an additional debt incurred after the original pledge?
b: Extending collateral: If someone pledges something for one hundred and then borrows another hundred and wants to use the original pledge as collateral for both debts, that is not allowed in the predominant position of ash-Shafi'i since the collateral is tied to the first debt. That is also the position of Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad. Mālik says it is permitted.

f: What are the rulings concerning selling collateral when the debt becomes due and is not paid, including delegation, judicial intervention, and loss of the proceeds held by a caretaker?
b: Selling collateral in the case of non-payment: If the pledger stipulates that the collateral can be sold if the debt is due and not paid, that is allowed by Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Mālik and Ahmad. Ash-Shafi'ī says that the pledgee is not permitted to sell the collateral himself. The pledger or his agent can sell it with the permission of the pledgee. If he refuses, the judge may oblige him to pay the debt or sell the collateral. Malik recommends that the collateral should be presented to a judge. If the pledgee does not do that and sells it, that is allowed. When the pledger appoints someone to sell the collateral when the debt is due and places it in his possession, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say that such delegation is valid. The pledger can annul that arrangement and dismiss him like other agents. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Malik says that he cannot. If both parties agree to deposit the collateral with a reputable person and the pledger stipulates that the person should sell it when payment is due, and he sells it and then the money is lost before the pledgee takes it, Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that it is the liability of the pledgee as if it was in his possession. Malik says that if the pledge is lost in the possession of the caretaker, it is the liability of the pledger as opposed to the pledgee. Ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say it is always the liability of the pledger unless the pledgee transgresses and then it is like a trust.

f: To whom does an increase that is separate from pledged property, such as offspring, fruit, or wool, belong according to the four Imams?
b: Increase in the value of collateral: In the case of increase in the collateral which is separate from it, like offspring, fruit, wool and other things, Mālik says they belong to the pledger. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that the increase is part of the collateral. Ash-Shafi'i says that all of it is separate from the collateral. Ahmad says that it belongs to the pledgee rather than the pledger.

f: How is the value of destroyed collateral determined when the parties agree on its description but disagree about its value?
b: Destruction of collateral: If a pledgee claims that the collateral has been destroyed and the parties agree on its value, there is no discussion. If they agree on its description but not its value, Mālik says that experts are asked about the price and action proceeds accordingly. Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that one accepts the word of the pledgee about the value when accompanied by an oath.

f: What are the rulings concerning placing a bankrupt or heavily indebted debtor under legal restraint and disposing of his property to pay creditors?
b: Legal restraint: Mālik, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say that a bankrupt, and a debtor when his debts overwhelm him, should be placed under legal restraint when his creditors request it, so that a judge can forbid him to dispose of his property to prevent his creditors being harmed. A judge can sell the property of a bankrupt if he refuses to sell it or divide it up between his creditors. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that a bankrupt should not be placed under legal restraint but rather imprisoned until he pays his debts. If he has property, the judge cannot dispose of it or sell it unless his property is in dirhams and his debt is in dirhams in which case the qādī can take it. If his debt is in dirhams and his property in dinars, it should be sold to pay the debt.

f: What are the limits on a bankrupt person's transactions after legal restraint, according to Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Mālik, ash-Shāfiʿī, and Aḥmad?
b: Limits of legal restraint: They disagree about a bankrupt disposing of his property after being placed under legal restraint. Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that there can be no legal restraint in any case. Even if a qadi decides on it, it should not be imposed. If restraint is imposed, transactions which cannot be nullified, like marriage, divorce and emancipation are carried out. Things which can be nullified, like sales, hiring, gifts and sadaqa, are invalid. Mālik says that transactions in respect of items of property through sales, gifts or emancipation, may not be carried out. Ash-Shafi'i has two positions: one is like Malik's and the second is that the transaction is valid but conditional. If his debts are paid, then the transactions are allowed. If they are not, then they are invalid, starting with the gift and then the sale. Ahmad says that none of his transactions are allowed except for emancipation.

f: What is the right of the original owner to unpaid goods found in the possession of a living or deceased bankrupt person?
b: Unpaid for goods: If a living bankrupt is in possession of some unpaid for goods and their owner takes them back, not having received any of their price, Malik, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say that the owner is more entitled to them than any other creditors and so he should take the goods rather than them. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that their owner is like any other creditor and that all the creditors should divide them between them. If the owner finds them after the bankrupt person has died and he has not received any money for them, ash-Shafi'i alone says that he is more entitled to them, as he would be if he was still alive. The other three say that he is like any other creditor.

f: How is a debt incurred by a bankrupt person after legal restraint treated in relation to the creditors whose claims caused the restraint?
b: Further debts: If a bankrupt incurs a further debt after legal restraint has been imposed, the debt is his responsibility, but the new creditor does not share with the other creditors on whose behalf the legal restraint was imposed, in the view of all but ash-Shafi'i, who says he does.

f: Can the home and necessary servants of a bankrupt person with no wealth be forcibly sold to pay his debts, according to the four Imams?
b: Seizure and sale of the home of a bankrupt: Can a bankrupt person with no wealth have his home and servants he needs forcibly sold to pay his debts? Abū Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Ahmad say that they should not be sold and Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that no property should be sold. Malik and ash-Shafi'i say that all such things should be sold.

f: What are the rulings concerning a debtor who has proven hardship, including release from prison, judicial intervention, and when evidence of hardship may be heard?
b: Cases of proven hardship: When someone's proven hardship is proven in the presence of a judge, can the judge come between him and his creditors? Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that the judge can release him from prison but not come between him and his creditors. They attend to him and may not stop him from transacting but may take the surplus of his earning by shares. Mālik, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say that the judge can release him from prison without the permission of his creditors and also intervene between him and them. He is not re-imprisoned, but the judge should oversee his conduct. They agree that evidence of hardship can be heard after imprisonment. They disagree about whether it can be heard before it. Malik, ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad say that it can be heard before. Abū Hanīfa's رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ position is that it can only be heard after it.

f: What are the recognized reasons for placing someone other than a bankrupt person under legal restraint, and what are the stated positions of the Imams concerning the age and signs of puberty?
b: Legal restraint for other than bankruptcy: They agree that other reasons for someone being under legal restraint are youth, slavedom and insanity. When a boy comes of age, but is not sane, his property should not be handed over to him. They disagree about when puberty occurs. Abū Hanīfa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says that for a boy it is a wet dream or ejaculation. If he does not experience that, it is when he reaches the age of seventeen or eighteen. A girl comes of age by menstruation, wet dreams, pregnancy or when she is seventeen. Mālik has no limit but his people say seventeen or eighteen.
